Null twin: same layer sizes and total parameter count, trained purely feedforward to predict the next frame with matched loss, no recurrent top-down/error-driven settling loop; compare occlusion-completion accuracy and residual spatial profile between the two.

mechanisms.statement: Two diffusing morphogens with local autocatalytic activation and longer-range inhibition, differing in diffusion rate, spontaneously break spatial symmetry into a stable periodic pattern (Turing pattern) whose wavelength depends only on the reaction-diffusion parameters, not on any pre-specified coordinate system. Cells read local morphogen concentration to set positional identity, so pattern re-forms adaptively when tissue is resized or damaged.
what_exists: activator and inhibitor concentration per cell
mechanisms.what_changes: Each step, concentrations update via discretized reaction terms (autocatalysis, mutual inhibition) plus diffusion (Laplacian) between neighboring cells; cell fate is set by thresholding local activator concentration.
mechanisms.what_persists: The emergent spatial wavelength/pattern type (stripes or spots) is stable across many steps once formed, robust to small perturbations.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: No within-lifetime selection; pattern stability across the parameter regime is an emergent dynamical property, though diffusion/reaction rates could themselves be subject to outer evolutionary selection.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: The pattern-generating mechanism re-executes identically whenever tissue is regrown, effectively 'reproducing' the pattern from the same rule set.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: None intrinsically; the mechanism is a fixed rule, though its parameters could be tuned by an outer learning/evolutionary loop.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: The same reaction-diffusion module transfers to tissues of different sizes, rescaling pattern count/wavelength according to domain size (scaling law), not requiring re-specification.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: After removing a portion of the tissue and letting it regrow, the pattern re-establishes with wavelength that scales with the new domain size according to the reaction-diffusion dispersion relation; a null twin using a fixed pre-computed positional lookup table (same steady-state pattern baked in, no diffusion feedback) fails to rescale and instead reproduces the original absolute pattern misaligned to the new domain size.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: a 1D row of N cells with activator/inhibitor reaction-diffusion dynamics tuned to produce a fixed number of stripes at size N0. Intervention: truncate the tissue to size N1 < N0 mid-simulation and let it re-equilibrate; measure resulting stripe count and wavelength as function of N1. Null twin: cells instead read from a static precomputed lookup table of activator values indexed by absolute position (matching the original N0 steady-state pattern exactly) with no diffusion or reaction update; after truncation to N1, compare pattern rescaling behavior between the dynamic and lookup-table systems.

mechanisms.statement: Multiple strategy types compete for a shared, finite, replenishing resource, and each type's growth rate is proportional to its resource-conversion efficiency minus a competition term from co-occurring types. This resource-mediated competitive dynamic selects for efficient or niche-differentiated strategies without any explicit fitness function beyond the shared resource constraint.
what_exists: set of strategy types with population density
shared resource pool with replenishment rate
per-type resource uptake and conversion efficiency
mechanisms.what_changes: Each step, resource is replenished, consumed by types proportional to density and uptake rate, and each type's density updates via a Lotka-Volterra-style growth term scaled by resource availability and interaction coefficients.
mechanisms.what_persists: Either a single dominant type (competitive exclusion) or a stable coexistence equilibrium, determined by the niche-overlap structure of interaction coefficients.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Types with higher resource-conversion efficiency relative to competitors, or with reduced niche overlap, are selected for persistence.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Each type reproduces proportional to its resource-scaled growth rate (birth-death process).
mechanisms.what_can_learn: No individual learning; the population-level outcome (which strategies persist) is the selection-driven inference of which strategies fit the resource landscape.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A winning strategy's parameters can seed populations in structurally similar new resource environments and predictably succeed if niche overlap with residents is low.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Time-to-fixation or coexistence outcome depends systematically on the efficiency/niche-overlap parameters; a null twin using a neutral (Moran-process) model where all types have identical growth rates regardless of efficiency shows fixation time scaling only with population size, uncorrelated with efficiency parameter, distinguishing selection from drift.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: two to four strategy types sharing one resource pool with logistic replenishment; efficiencies and interaction coefficients set experimentally. Intervention: vary the niche-overlap matrix and measure whether coexistence or exclusion results, and correlate fixation probability with efficiency rank. Null twin: identical population sizes and resource replenishment, but growth increments assigned by a neutral Moran process (random type chosen to reproduce/die each step regardless of efficiency); compare fixation-time distributions and their correlation (or lack thereof) with the efficiency parameter between the two systems.

mechanisms.statement: Genomes evolve under a mutation operator combining point mutation with occasional segmental duplication, where duplicated segments can subsequently diverge independently of the original. This produces redundant genetic material that can drift neutrally with respect to current fitness while preserving the original function, later enabling adaptive divergence without loss of the ancestral trait.
what_exists: genome as a linear sequence/graph of modules
genotype-to-phenotype map with degeneracy (multiple genotypes -> same phenotype)
mechanisms.what_changes: Each generation, genomes undergo point mutation at fixed rate and, at a lower rate, segment duplication; duplicated copies then accumulate independent point mutations across subsequent generations.
mechanisms.what_persists: Phenotypic function is conserved across neutral genotypic changes (neutral network); standing cryptic genetic diversity accumulates in duplicated, currently non-essential segments.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Selection acts on phenotype only; genotypic variation within a neutral network (including duplicated segments) is invisible to selection until an environmental shift makes divergent copies functionally relevant.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Standard sexual/asexual reproduction with the mutation operator applied each generation.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The population's evolvability increases over generations (facilitated variation): a population-level capacity to respond faster to future environmental shifts.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Duplicated, diverged modules can be recombined or co-opted (exapted) to build new phenotypic functions when needed.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Following a sudden environmental shift that requires a new function, populations with duplication-enabled mutation show a shorter and less variable time-to-adaptation than a null twin; measured via distribution of generations-to-fitness-recovery.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: a population of genomes mapping via a many-to-one function to a phenotype vector under selection on a fitness landscape; the environment shifts fitness peak at generation T. Intervention: run evolution with the duplication+point-mutation operator and record time-to-recovery of peak fitness after the shift. Null twin: identical genome length distribution and total mutation-rate variance, but using point mutation only (mutation rate rescaled so total per-generation phenotypic variance matches the duplication condition, no duplication events); compare post-shift adaptation-time distributions between the two.

mechanisms.statement: A network's global connectivity is controlled by a single parameter (edge probability or rewiring probability) and exhibits a sharp percolation phase transition at a critical value, below which the network fragments into small disconnected components and above which a giant component spans most nodes. Only above this threshold can information injected at one node reliably reach distal nodes, gating whether the network functions as an integrated computational substrate.
what_exists: edges added according to control parameter p
signal injected at a source node
measurement of information/activity at distal nodes
mechanisms.what_changes: Edges are added/removed as p is swept; network topology (giant component size, path lengths) changes correspondingly; a fixed dynamical process (e.g., diffusion or spiking) runs on top of the current topology.
mechanisms.what_persists: Once p exceeds the critical value, the giant component persists as the dominant structural feature across further small perturbations to p.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Not applicable directly; the law is purely structural/dynamical, though it gates which downstream learned functions (needing global integration) are achievable.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Not applicable.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: A readout trained to use distal-node activity only succeeds in learning integrative tasks when p is above the percolation threshold.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Signal correlations between distant node pairs, once established, transfer information regardless of specific task, but only in the connected regime.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Mutual information between a fixed source node and a distal node, measured as a function of p, shows a sharp transition near p_c with finite-size scaling exponents matching percolation theory; a null twin with the same average degree but a regular lattice topology (no random rewiring) shows a smooth, gradual increase in mutual information with p and no sharp threshold or scaling collapse.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: N nodes, edges added at random with probability p (Erdos-Renyi); a diffusive/relay dynamic propagates an injected signal from a fixed source node. Intervention: sweep p across the theoretical percolation threshold p_c = 1/N for this topology, measuring giant-component size and source-to-distal mutual information at multiple network sizes to test finite-size scaling. Null twin: same N and same average degree achieved instead by a ring lattice with local rewiring limited to nearest neighbors plus the same number of total edges added deterministically (not randomly), preserving average degree and edge count but lacking random long-range shortcuts; compare the sharpness/threshold behavior of source-to-distal mutual information between the two.

mechanisms.statement: Each unit in a recurrent network is permanently fixed as either strictly excitatory or strictly inhibitory (the sign of all its outgoing weights is fixed at initialization and enforced by projection after every update), while weight magnitudes remain trainable. This constraint reduces the effective solution space available to learning and is expected to bias the network toward different, more structurally interpretable and differently robust solutions than an unconstrained network of equal size.
what_exists: recurrent network units each tagged excitatory or inhibitory
mechanisms.what_changes: Standard gradient update on weight magnitudes each step, followed by a projection step that clips any weight whose sign would flip back to zero (or its minimum magnitude with correct sign), enforcing the fixed-sign constraint throughout training.
mechanisms.what_persists: The excitatory/inhibitory identity of each unit and the resulting motif statistics (e.g., E/I ratio, characteristic connection patterns) remain fixed while magnitudes adapt.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Among all networks that could solve the task, only those reachable within the sign-constrained subspace are found by gradient descent; this constrains which dynamical solutions (e.g., specific oscillatory or attractor structures) are discovered.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Not applicable directly.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The network learns to perform the task using only weight-magnitude adjustments within the fixed sign structure.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Solutions found under the constraint may generalize differently to task variants or perturbations than unconstrained solutions, due to their different inductive bias.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: For networks trained to matched task performance, targeted lesioning of inhibitory units produces a qualitatively different (typically more catastrophic, less graceful) degradation pattern in the sign-constrained network than in a null twin (identical architecture, same training procedure, but no sign constraint, i.e., weights free to take any sign) lesioned at matched-magnitude units; the resulting weight-magnitude distributions also differ systematically (e.g., heavier tail in constrained case).
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: a small recurrent network trained to perform a working-memory or oscillation task via gradient descent, with half its units pre-designated excitatory and half inhibitory. Intervention: train with sign constraint enforced by post-update projection; then lesion (zero out) the inhibitory units' outgoing weights and measure task performance degradation and dynamical stability. Null twin: identical architecture and training loss, no sign constraint (free signs), trained to matched final task performance; lesion an equal-count, magnitude-matched subset of units and compare the shape and severity of the resulting performance/dynamics degradation curve between constrained and unconstrained networks.

mechanisms.statement: A recurrent network of nonlinear units maintains its global coupling strength near a critical value (edge of chaos, where the largest Lyapunov exponent is approximately zero) via a local homeostatic gain-adjustment rule, rather than a fixed or externally-tuned coupling. This self-tuned criticality jointly maximizes both short-term memory capacity and input-separation ability, providing a general-purpose substrate usable across many downstream readout tasks.
what_exists: recurrent network of nonlinear units with local gain parameter per unit
homeostatic rule targeting a set-point of local activity variance
mechanisms.what_changes: Each step, units update via nonlinear recurrent dynamics driven by input; each unit's local gain adjusts slowly to bring its activity variance toward a homeostatic target, indirectly moving the effective coupling g toward the critical value for the current input statistics.
mechanisms.what_persists: The dynamical regime (near-zero Lyapunov exponent) is maintained as an attracting operating point of the homeostatic feedback, persisting despite changes in input statistics.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: No explicit selection process; the homeostatic rule itself acts as a local, task-independent optimization toward the critical regime.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Not applicable.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The homeostatic gain rule learns/tracks the appropriate coupling without any supervised signal (unsupervised self-tuning); separately, a linear readout learns specific tasks from the network's states.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: The same underlying network, once at criticality, supports multiple different linear readouts (multiple tasks) with high performance, i.e., the representation transfers across tasks better than off-critical regimes.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Sweeping the coupling parameter g and measuring both delayed-recall memory capacity and stimulus-separation capacity shows both jointly peak near the same critical g, and the homeostatic system's effective g tracks this peak as input statistics change; a null twin with a fixed (non-adaptive) coupling value chosen to match the average dynamical range but without local homeostatic feedback fails to re-track the peak when input statistics shift, showing degraded joint memory/separation performance after the shift.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: a recurrent network of tanh units receiving a time-varying scalar input stream with two different statistical regimes (regime A, then regime B) presented in sequence; a local homeostatic gain-adjustment rule updates each unit's gain based on a target activity variance. Intervention: measure memory capacity (linear reconstruction of past input) and separation capacity (distinguishability of nearby input trajectories) as functions of swept fixed g, and separately track these metrics over time for the homeostatically-adapting network across the regime A-to-B transition. Null twin: same network and readout tasks, but coupling g is fixed at the value optimal for regime A (no ongoing homeostatic adjustment); compare memory/separation performance of the adaptive vs. fixed-g network specifically during and after the transition to regime B.

mechanisms.statement: System state is tracked by a recursive Bayesian update in which a compact sufficient statistic (mean and covariance) is propagated forward by a predict step and corrected by an observation-weighted update (Kalman gain). The gain automatically balances trust in the model's prediction against trust in the new observation according to their relative uncertainties. This produces optimal-in-variance tracking without ever storing the raw observation history.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: the gain value that minimizes posterior variance at each step
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the noise parameters Q,R can be fit by maximum likelihood/EM over observed trajectories
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: learned Q,R generalize to new trajectories generated by the same or structurally similar linear system
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: when observation noise R changes mid-run, the optimal filter's gain and posterior variance shift immediately to match, while a fixed-gain exponential smoother with the same average gain lags or overshoots for several steps
mechanisms.minimal_world: a 1D linear-Gaussian tracking task where a hidden scalar random walk is observed with noise; intervention: abruptly change the observation noise variance partway through the sequence; null twin: an exponential moving average with a fixed smoothing constant chosen to match the Kalman filter's steady-state gain before the change, which cannot adapt when noise changes.

mechanisms.statement: Data from an exponential-family source can be losslessly compressed for the purpose of prediction into a fixed-size sufficient statistic, discarding the raw sequence entirely. Only the statistic needs to be updated as new data arrives, via a simple additive rule. Any predictive query about future data can be answered from the statistic alone with no loss relative to using the full raw history.

mechanisms.what_persists: the sufficient statistic T, whose size does not grow with n
mechanisms.what_is_selected: the minimal statistic satisfying the Fisher-Neyman factorization for the assumed family
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: T can regenerate the predictive distribution over future data equivalently to the full history
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a point estimate theta-hat derived from T
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: statistics from independent data batches can be summed/merged across agents to pool evidence without sharing raw data
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: predictive accuracy on held-out future observations using only T equals accuracy using the full raw sequence, whereas a fixed-size non-sufficient summary (e.g., last k observations) shows degrading accuracy as n grows
mechanisms.minimal_world: a Bernoulli coin-flip generator; one agent stores only (heads count, total count), another stores only the last k flips; intervention: shuffle the flip order (exchangeable, statistic unaffected) and increase n; null twin: the fixed-window agent, matched in memory size, whose predictions degrade relative to the sufficient-statistic agent as n increases.

mechanisms.statement: Fitting under a combined loss of data-fit plus a penalty on parameter magnitude creates a pressure toward biased-but-lower-variance estimates whenever the penalty strength is tuned by held-out risk. This produces a characteristic U-shaped generalization-error curve as a function of penalty strength, with a nonzero optimum whenever noise is present relative to signal.

mechanisms.what_persists: the shrunk estimate w-hat(lambda) across the optimization
mechanisms.what_is_selected: the value of lambda minimizing held-out risk
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the mapping from noise-to-signal ratio to optimal shrinkage intensity
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: an optimal lambda* learned on one dataset transfers to new datasets with matched dimensionality and noise level
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: test error vs lambda traces a U-shape with a nonzero minimum under noise, whereas an unregularized (lambda=0) fit shows monotonically worsening generalization as feature dimension approaches or exceeds sample size
mechanisms.minimal_world: linear regression with p close to or exceeding n, where most features are pure noise and a few carry signal; intervention: increase the noise variance of the response; null twin: the same setup fit by unregularized least squares (or pseudo-inverse), matched on training loss but lacking the shrinkage penalty.

mechanisms.statement: A pair of conjugate hyperparameters can serve as a complete, fixed-size memory of an arbitrarily long history of binary observations. Each observation updates the hyperparameters by a simple increment, and the resulting posterior predictive distribution is identical to what would be computed from the full raw history. Hyperparameters from independent observers can be merged additively to pool evidence.

mechanisms.minimal_world: a sequence of Bernoulli trials with a fixed true rate; intervention: interleave and then merge the (alpha,beta) memories of two independently updating agents observing disjoint subsequences; null twin: an agent maintaining a fixed-length raw window of the last k observations instead of the sufficient hyperparameters, matched on memory size.

mechanisms.statement: A population of weighted particles approximating a posterior distribution is periodically resampled with probability proportional to likelihood weight, so that particles consistent with new observations are copied (reproduce) while inconsistent particles are eliminated. This selection step prevents weight degeneracy and keeps the particle population an effective approximation of the true posterior under nonlinear, non-Gaussian dynamics.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: particles whose state predicts the observed data well survive and are copied; low-likelihood particles are eliminated

mechanisms.what_can_learn: the population-level estimate of the hidden state improves in accuracy as effective particle diversity is maintained across nonlinear regimes
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a converged particle cloud can seed (warm-start) a filter tracking a related but shifted dynamical regime
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: effective sample size stays bounded and tracking error remains low with resampling, while a matched importance-sampling scheme without a resampling/selection step shows exploding weight variance and estimator collapse (particle degeneracy) on the same observation sequence
mechanisms.minimal_world: a nonlinear 1D bearings-only tracking task; intervention: introduce a sudden regime change in the hidden dynamics; null twin: an importance sampler using the identical weighting update but never resampling particles, tracking the same data stream.

mechanisms.statement: Perturbed variant datasets generated by sampling with replacement from an original dataset induce variation in fitted model parameters that approximates the true sampling distribution of an estimator. This variation can be used to estimate the estimator's variance without any analytic derivation, and is distinct from perturbing the estimate directly with unstructured noise.

mechanisms.statement: A sequence of weak learners is trained where each subsequent learner is fit on a reweighted version of the data that up-weights examples the ensemble so far gets wrong, and each learner's vote is weighted by its own accuracy. This adaptively concentrates learning capacity on residual errors, producing training error that decreases characteristically fast compared to non-adaptive resampling.

mechanisms.statement: An encoder can be tuned along a rate-distortion tradeoff to compress an input into a representation that retains only the information relevant to predicting a target, discarding irrelevant input variation. Sweeping the tradeoff parameter traces a frontier of achievable (compression, relevance) pairs that dominates representations chosen blind to the target.

mechanisms.statement: Restricting a model class to those whose joint distribution over a sequence is invariant under permutation of indices forces the representation to factor through a latent parameter with an order-independent mixing distribution (de Finetti representation). mechanisms.statement: Iteratively alternating between computing soft posterior responsibilities for latent structure given current parameters, and updating parameters to maximize expected complete-data likelihood under those responsibilities, causes latent structure to emerge from unlabeled data through a monotonic self-consistent refinement process. mechanisms.statement: In entropy-regularized optimal control (KL/path-integral control), the Pontryagin costate (value gradient) is exactly the natural parameter of the maximum-entropy trajectory distribution. When the cost-to-go tensor V[s,t] is CP/Tucker-decomposed, the same low-rank factors simultaneously determine the feedback control law and the moment constraints of the maxent path measure, so a backward HJB sweep and a forward moment-matching sweep must update the identical factor set. This forces a specific coupling: any perturbation of a factor entry produces a predicted policy shift derivable purely from the maxent normalization equation, without re-solving HJB.
mechanisms.what_exists: state grid s, time index t, cost-to-go tensor V[s,t], CP factor matrices (A_state, A_time) of rank R, temperature λ, action set a
mechanisms.what_changes: backward soft-min HJB recursion updates V; ALS refits (A_state, A_time) to the updated V each step, and the reconstructed V simultaneously serves as the maxent natural parameter for the trajectory distribution
mechanisms.what_persists: the rank-R factor structure and the identity mapping between costate and natural parameter across the backward sweep
mechanisms.what_is_selected: components that most reduce ALS reconstruction loss weighted by expected cost reduction survive refitting
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: factor slices can be duplicated across adjacent time steps when temporally smooth
mechanisms.what_can_learn: temperature λ and factor entries adapt online from sampled trajectories
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A_state (state geometry) reused across different cost functions with the same dynamics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: perturbing one factor entry by δ predicts, via the closed-form maxent normalization derivative, a specific policy shift; a system with independently fit value function and policy (no shared factor) shows no such linear correspondence between the perturbation and the realized shift
mechanisms.minimal_world: 5x5 gridworld, T=10, cost = distance to a moving goal; ground truth is tabular HJB. Fit CP rank-3 factors to V at each backward step via ALS and derive the policy from the reconstruction. Intervention: perturb one component of A_state and compare (a) the policy shift predicted from the maxent/costate identity formula against (b) the policy shift from re-solving HJB with the perturbed low-rank V substituted as the stage-cost surrogate. Null twin: replace CP-ALS with an arbitrary autoencoder of matching compression ratio and reconstruction error whose latent code is not tied to the costate identity; the same perturbation should fail to predict the policy shift.

mechanisms.statement: A Tucker decomposition splits the joint state-action-task occupancy tensor into mode matrices (state embedding, action embedding) shared across tasks and a task-specific core tensor. Maximum entropy supplies the rule for turning shared-factor plus core into a valid stochastic policy; optimal control supplies the loss that determines what information the core must carry. Transfer becomes literally the reuse of mode matrices while only the core is refit to a new cost function.
mechanisms.what_exists: shared mode matrices U_state, U_action, per-task core tensor G_k, per-task cost function c_k, temperature λ
mechanisms.what_changes: core G_k is refit by minimizing expected cost under the maxent policy induced by (U_state, U_action, G_k); mode matrices update slower, shared across tasks
mechanisms.what_persists: U_state and U_action across the task sequence
mechanisms.what_is_selected: core configurations that minimize task-specific expected cost at fixed shared factors
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a new task instantiates a fresh core tensor initialized by nearest-neighbor task core
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the core tensor per task; occasionally the shared mode matrices via slow gradient averaged across tasks
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: U_state, U_action transfer zero-shot to a new task, requiring only core refitting
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: learning speed (trials to reach cost threshold) on a new task with frozen shared factors vs. a control condition that refits a full unstructured tensor from scratch; the shared-factor condition should show far fewer required samples specifically when tasks differ only in cost, not in state geometry
mechanisms.minimal_world: A family of 6x6 gridworlds sharing the same transition/state geometry but different goal locations (tasks). Train Tucker factors on tasks 1-5, freeze U_state/U_action, and refit only G_6 on task 6, measuring trials-to-convergence. Null twin: an unstructured full-rank value table refit from scratch on task 6 but pre-initialized with the average of the first 5 tasks' tables (matching prior information content but no factor sharing structure) — should converge slower or to a worse asymptote.

mechanisms.statement: Restricting the maxent trajectory distribution to match only the moments representable by a rank-R tensor factorization of the state-action occupancy measure creates a bottleneck whose control-cost penalty has a specific functional form in R (rather than an arbitrary compression penalty). Maxent alone does not specify which moments to constrain; the tensor factorization specifies exactly which, and optimal control supplies the metric that reveals the truncation's cost.

mechanisms.what_changes: R is swept as an experimental parameter; for each R the occupancy tensor is projected onto its best rank-R CP approximation and the corresponding maxent policy is computed and executed
mechanisms.what_persists: the environment's true generative rank R* across the sweep
mechanisms.what_is_selected: no selection; this is a measurement mechanism
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable

mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the fitted J(R) curve transfers as a predictive formula to new environments sharing similar tensor mode structure
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: J(R) should show a sharp elbow near R=R*, unlike a generic complexity penalty (e.g., L2 weight decay on an unstructured policy table) which produces a smooth monotonic curve with no elbow tied to the environment's rank
mechanisms.minimal_world: Construct a synthetic environment whose true occupancy tensor has exact CP rank R*=4 (built by summing 4 rank-1 outer products with known coefficients). Sweep R=1..8, fit rank-R maxent policies, measure realized cost. Null twin: an environment with the same total variance/entropy in occupancy but generated by a dense random tensor (no low-rank structure); sweeping R here should show smooth decay with no elbow, matching first and second moments of the true-rank environment but lacking the mechanism.

mechanisms.statement: Tensor rank R is not fixed but is driven by a pressure minimizing J(R) = expected control cost under the rank-R maxent policy + β·R (a description-length penalty on factors). This differs from ordinary regularization because both the cost term and the complexity term are counted in the same units (nats of entropy vs. nats of description) only once maxent supplies the free-energy accounting and control supplies the cost term.

mechanisms.what_changes: R increments when marginal cost reduction from adding a rank-1 component exceeds β; decrements when a component's marginal cost contribution falls below β
mechanisms.what_persists: β across the run, unless itself annealed
mechanisms.what_is_selected: components whose removal least increases J are pruned first
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: components can be cloned with small jitter to test if splitting reduces J further
mechanisms.what_can_learn: R and the factor entries co-adapt through the threshold rule
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the final rank R* and component set transfer as an initialization prior to a related task
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: final R should track the environment's true generative rank as β is varied on a log grid, producing a plateau at R=R*; a naive AIC/BIC-style penalty applied to an arbitrary (non-tensor) parameterization of the policy should not show a plateau tied to R*

Over time this yields internal states that anticipate incoming data rather than merely reacting to it.

mechanisms.minimal_world: A small vision-like network trained on oriented-edge stimuli with a decaying plasticity gate; simulate monocular-deprivation-like blanking of one input channel at early, mid, or late points in the decay schedule, then restore input and probe orientation-selectivity. Null twin: identical architecture, inputs, and error signal but with the plasticity gate held constant at a value matching total cumulative plasticity of the decaying-gate run, showing full recovery regardless of deprivation timing.

mechanisms.statement: A population of noisy units independently estimates the same variable; a robust consensus aggregate (e.g., trimmed mean) is computed from all estimates for downstream use, and each unit slowly recalibrates its own bias toward reducing its residual from the consensus. This produces a self-correcting, redundant code whose accuracy and robustness exceed any single constituent unit's.
what_exists: population of M noisy units each estimating variable v
mechanisms.what_changes: Each step, unit i outputs y_i = v + noise_i + bias_i; consensus c = robust_aggregate(y_1..y_M); bias_i updates slowly toward reducing (y_i - c).
mechanisms.what_persists: The redundancy factor M and the calibrated bias configuration persist as the stable operating point of the ensemble.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Units with smaller systematic bias (more consistent with consensus) contribute more reliably; in a competitive variant, low-reliability units can be pruned and replaced.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: The whole ensemble configuration (biases, count M) can be copied into a new instance to bootstrap error-corrected coding immediately.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: Each unit's bias parameter is learned online from consensus residuals; the ensemble learns a self-consistent calibrated code.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A calibrated ensemble can be transplanted into a related context with similar noise statistics requiring minimal re-calibration.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Decoding accuracy degrades gracefully (roughly linearly) as an increasing fraction of units is lesioned, rather than failing abruptly.
mechanisms.minimal_world: M=20 noisy sensors reporting a scalar v(t) plus independent noise and slowly drifting unit-specific bias; consensus readout via trimmed mean drives a steering task. Progressively lesion increasing fractions of units and measure the performance decay curve. Null twin: a single unit with noise variance equal to 1/M of the ensemble's effective noise (matched aggregate accuracy when undamaged), which fails completely upon its own lesion instead of degrading gracefully.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: checks embedded in appropriately-sized (neither vanishing nor runaway) avalanches are reinforced; unused or catastrophically overloaded check placements are pruned or amplified respectively
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: individual parity checks are duplicated onto neighboring fragile sites, giving checks a literal birth-death/copy dynamic
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the population-level redundancy profile converges toward a spatially-varying allocation matched to local noise exposure, learned without central computation
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a redundancy profile equilibrated under one noise environment should retain adaptive advantage (faster re-stabilization) when transplanted into a new environment with similar avalanche statistics but a different exact noise trace
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the lag/hysteresis structure between noise injection and redundancy change is mediated by avalanche propagation delay; contrast with a null twin where redundancy responds directly to locally measured noise rate, which should equilibrate similarly under simple noise but diverge when noise and realized impact decouple spatially
mechanisms.minimal_world: a ring of N sites with baseline checks, heterogeneous noise injection, and the mutation operator applied every W steps. Null twin: identical ring and toppling rule, but redundancy mutation driven directly by locally measured noise-injection frequency rather than realized avalanche size, matched under simple noise but diverging when a site is protected by a distant neighbor's redundancy.

mechanisms.statement: The world is a stack of L nested code levels where level ℓ's decoded blocks are level ℓ+1's raw symbols, and decode failures at level ℓ inject noise events into level ℓ+1; each level independently runs the syndrome-driven toppling dynamics. The rule that cross-level coupling occurs only through actual decode failure (not a fixed schedule) forces each level's phase-transition point to align with the others, producing a single shared multi-level critical point rather than L independent ones.
what_exists: L layers each with its own Tanner graph and syndrome-load state
fixed block partition mapping level ℓ blocks to level ℓ+1 symbols
mechanisms.what_changes: within-layer toppling as in the base dynamical law; additionally, unresolved syndrome at layer ℓ after allotted rounds injects a noise event into the corresponding block at layer ℓ+1
mechanisms.what_persists: the fixed nested block-partition structure across layers
mechanisms.what_is_selected: operating regimes where failure-cascade rates are mutually consistent across levels persist; mismatched regimes either saturate into permanent failure or freeze into unused redundancy
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not directly, though extended versions could allow whole blocks to be duplicated as offspring across trajectories
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the stack can self-consistently settle into per-level noise thresholds that place all levels near their own critical points simultaneously, without any single controller computing this alignment
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: swapping one layer's code for a different code of the same rate but different degree distribution should preserve overall stack criticality if alignment is structural (coupling-driven) rather than code-specific
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: simultaneous divergence of avalanche-size distributions across all L levels at a single shared noise value, versus a null twin where inter-layer noise is injected at a matched average rate via an independent process unrelated to actual decode failure, which should produce L independent critical points instead of one shared point
mechanisms.minimal_world: a 3-level stack of 16-symbol LDPC-like blocks with decode-failure-triggered inter-level noise injection. Null twin: identical stack and matched average injection rate, but injection scheduled by an independent Poisson process rather than by actual decode failures, severing the causal link between levels' internal criticality states.

mechanisms.statement: A population of local codeword patches survives each generation only if it lies within Hamming distance d of some valid codeword (sufficient satisfied checks); failed patches are replaced by mutated copies of surviving neighbors. As constraint density is swept across the constraint-satisfaction (SAT/UNSAT) threshold, survival fraction undergoes a sharp phase transition, while repeated turnover near that threshold produces bursty extinction/replacement events resembling SOC avalanches. This mechanism only exists jointly: the phase transition needs the check structure, and the avalanches need the repeated selection-replacement cycle.
mechanisms.what_changes: each generation, patches below the survival threshold die and empty slots are refilled by mutated copies of a randomly chosen surviving neighbor; constraint density can be slowly increased to sweep the SAT/UNSAT transition
mechanisms.what_persists: the check structure defining satisfaction and the partially-inherited symbol content of surviving lineages
mechanisms.what_is_selected: patches within a Hamming ball of any valid codeword (not a specific one), allowing multiple coexisting codeword-basin 'species'
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: surviving patches reproduce via mutated local copying into empty neighboring slots
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a constraint-density controller can learn to hover near the SAT/UNSAT boundary using feedback on extinction-burst rate, producing SOC co-located with the phase transition
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: lineages evolved near one code's SAT/UNSAT boundary should re-adapt faster when moved to a differently-structured but same-rate code, versus lineages evolved far from threshold
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: extinction-burst size distribution shows a power-law peak sharply located at the theoretical satisfiability threshold for the check ensemble, shifting predictably with check-degree distribution, unlike a null twin with a check-free random fitness landscape matched in mean/variance which shows only a smooth crossover
mechanisms.minimal_world: a ring population of length-20 binary strings with degree-3 parity checks (random 3-XOR-SAT-like), constraint density swept as control parameter, survival/reproduction as described. Null twin: identical population/topology/mutation, but fitness drawn from a random Gaussian landscape matched in mean and variance to the real fitness at each density, removing actual SAT/UNSAT structure.

mechanisms.statement: Each parity check carries a slowly-decaying weight that is reinforced every time it participates in a toppling avalanche, and this weight modulates the local toppling threshold, so regions with a history of large avalanches become path-dependently more resistant or permissive. This produces hysteresis in the location and shape of the critical point across up/down sweeps of the noise-rate control parameter, a signature only possible when both code structure (something to weight) and repeated criticality (something to remember) coexist.
what_exists: site-level toppling threshold modulated by neighboring check weights
mechanisms.what_changes: w_c increases by a fixed increment whenever check c participates in a topple, and decays multiplicatively otherwise; local threshold is a function of base threshold plus neighboring weights
mechanisms.what_persists: the check topology and the slowly-varying weight field, which persists across many avalanches on a longer timescale than any single cascade
mechanisms.what_is_selected: no explicit selection; regions of accumulated weight become de facto protected or preferred avalanche corridors depending on coupling sign
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the weight field is a slow-learning trace encoding a spatial map of recurring criticality, i.e., an experience-dependent representation of the system's own fault lines
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a weight field trained under one spatial noise pattern, transplanted onto a fresh lattice under a statistically similar but different noise pattern, should reduce transient large-avalanche incidence faster than an untrained uniform-weight lattice
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: sweeping noise rate up then down produces a nonzero-area hysteresis loop in the order parameter (fraction of satisfied checks or mean avalanche size), whereas a null twin with fixed thresholds and no reinforcement/decay predicts a reversible, non-hysteretic transition
mechanisms.minimal_world: the 2D LDPC-like sandpile lattice with added per-check weight dynamics, slowly sweeping noise rate p up and back down across the critical region, recording the order-parameter loop. Null twin: identical lattice, code, and sweep protocol but static thresholds with no reinforcement or decay.

mechanisms.statement: A coarse-graining encoder compresses each codeword block into a smaller summary retaining only the κn bits most correlated with unsatisfied checks, and only this summary propagates during avalanches. The joint prediction is that the avalanche-size cutoff is set by a combined quantity involving both compression ratio κ and code rate R, a quantity that does not exist without both the code and the bottleneck present simultaneously.
what_exists: bottleneck encoder producing κn-bit summaries prioritized by syndrome-relevance
mechanisms.what_changes: at each propagation step the encoder recomputes which κn bits are most correlated with unsatisfied checks and only those propagate, the rest being dropped and lost to the cascade
mechanisms.what_persists: the block partition structure and the prioritization rule for bit selection, while summary content itself is transient
mechanisms.what_is_selected: no direct agent selection; κ and R are swept as external control parameters to locate qualitative changes in cutoff behavior
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the bit-prioritization rule can itself be adapted over many avalanches to maximize decoding success at fixed κ, an explicit representation-learning process driven by avalanche feedback
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a learned bit-relevance map trained under one code/rate should partially transfer to a different code instance with the same degree distribution, testing whether the learned relevance captures generalizable structure
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: avalanche cutoff s*(κ,R) collapses onto a single curve depending on (R−κ) rather than κ and R independently, whereas a null twin dropping a random κn-subset shows cutoff depending only on κ with no dependence on R
mechanisms.minimal_world: the LDPC sandpile substrate with propagation routed through a syndrome-prioritized κn-bit bottleneck; sweep κ and R independently, measure avalanche cutoff. Null twin: identical topology and toppling rule but the bottleneck drops a random κn-subset of bits each step, matched in compression ratio and cost but not information content.

mechanisms.statement: Starting from a minimal seed graph, new checks and edges are added preferentially at nodes that recently experienced large avalanches rather than at nodes with high current degree, so the graph's mature degree distribution is a product of its own criticality history. The prediction is that this avalanche-seeded growth converges to the degree distribution known from coding theory to sit at the belief-propagation decoding threshold, meaning development and the phase transition are the same emergent fixed point.
mechanisms.what_changes: each growth epoch adds G new edges/checks attaching with probability proportional to a softmax over avalanche-participation counters, then toppling dynamics runs for a window and counters update, repeating over many epochs
mechanisms.what_persists: the accumulated graph structure from earlier epochs, since growth is irreversible in the basic version
mechanisms.what_is_selected: no explicit selection in the simplest version; degree-distribution convergence is the selected outcome of repeated growth-instability feedback
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable in the basic version, though extended versions could copy whole graph trajectories with mutation and select for fastest convergence to threshold
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the topology structurally 'learns' the degree distribution yielding threshold-adjacent decoding purely from local instability feedback, without ever computing density evolution explicitly
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a graph grown under one noise regime should re-converge faster to a new appropriate degree distribution under a changed regime, compared to a graph grown by pure random attachment, testing reusable structural plasticity
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the converged degree distribution's predicted density-evolution threshold coincides with the noise level at which the growth process's own avalanche statistics actually go critical, whereas a null twin using plain degree-proportional preferential attachment converges to a degree distribution whose theoretical threshold need not coincide with its actual operating point
mechanisms.minimal_world: start with 8 variable and 4 check nodes, grow to ~200 nodes via avalanche-seeded attachment interleaved with toppling/noise-injection dynamics; compare final degree distribution's threshold to observed critical noise level. Null twin: identical growth schedule and budget but attachment probability proportional to current degree, matched in total edges/nodes/timing but severing the growth-instability link.

mechanisms.statement: Stress can pass from a site to a neighbor only across an edge belonging to a currently-violated parity check; satisfied checks act as insulators blocking propagation entirely rather than merely attenuating it. Because check-satisfaction status changes moment-to-moment as an avalanche proceeds, the effective propagation topology fluctuates on top of a fixed underlying graph, and this predicts that critical exponents of the resulting transition depend on code parameters rather than being fixed by lattice dimensionality alone.
what_exists: fixed Tanner graph with edges labeled satisfied/violated at each instant
mechanisms.what_changes: at each propagation step stress moves only across currently-violated edges, after which satisfied/violated status of all touched checks is recomputed, opening or closing paths for the next step within the same avalanche
mechanisms.what_persists: the underlying fixed graph, whose edges are only gated open/closed and never structurally added or removed
mechanisms.what_is_selected: no explicit agent selection; avalanche paths are moment-to-moment selected by which checks happen to be violated, producing a path-dependent effective topology
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: none intrinsic; this is a bottom-level interaction primitive on which mutation, memory, and developmental mechanisms above can be built
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the quantitative relationship between code rate/degree distribution and resulting critical exponents should be a transferable, class-universal law testable across different codes sharing graph connectivity
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: critical exponents (e.g., avalanche size-duration scaling) shift systematically with code rate/degree distribution at fixed lattice connectivity, whereas a null twin with edges gated open at a matched average fraction independent of real check status shows exponents fixed by lattice dimensionality alone
mechanisms.minimal_world: a fixed 2D nearest-neighbor lattice overlaid with an LDPC-like check structure, stress propagating only through violated-check edges; vary code rate/degree distribution at fixed lattice connectivity and measure avalanche exponents. Null twin: identical lattice with the same average open-edge fraction assigned by an independent random gate each step rather than by actual check-violation status.

  "distinguishing_observable": "incidence of instability/divergence episodes and long-run performance variance for periodic idempotent retraction versus continuous L2 shrinkage regularization matched in average parameter-correction magnitude",
  "minimal_world": "An adaptive pole-placement controller for a plant with slowly drifting parameters, where naive recursive least-squares updates occasionally produce unstable closed-loop gains. Null twin: identical drift and identical average magnitude of parameter correction, but correction is applied as continuous weight decay rather than discrete idempotent projection onto the stable-gain set, matching the nuisance statistic of 'average shrinkage' while lacking the idempotent well-formed-subcategory guarantee."
}

mechanisms.statement: Adaptation is required to be a functor F from a category of tasks (objects = plant parameterizations, morphisms = task transformations) to a category of controllers (objects = gain vectors, morphisms = achievable adaptation moves). The functoriality law F(g∘f)=F(g)∘F(f) is enforced as an extra term in the adaptation loss, so composing two learned adaptations must equal the adaptation learned directly for the composite task. Violations of this law are treated as detectable interference/forgetting rather than tolerated noise.
mechanisms.what_changes: controller parameters update via the standard adaptation law plus a gradient term penalizing ||F(g∘f)-F(g)∘F(f)|| on sampled morphism pairs
mechanisms.what_persists: the functor table/rule mapping task morphisms to controller morphisms, reused across new task instances
mechanisms.what_is_selected: controllers/adaptation rules with lowest composition-violation error across many sampled morphism chains
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the learned functor (mapping rule) can be copied wholesale to initialize a new controller instance on an unseen but related task
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the adaptation-law's learning-rate/shape parameters, tuned specifically to minimize functoriality violation
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: competence on a composite task inferred purely from competence on its factors, without direct training on the composite
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: divergence between (adapt-on-A then adapt-on-B) and (adapt directly on A-then-B) for a plain adaptive controller versus the functorially-constrained one; the constrained version should show near-zero divergence, the plain one large divergence
mechanisms.minimal_world: A chain of linear plants whose parameters drift according to a small set of composable transformations (e.g., gain scale, gain shift); the controller is a state-feedback gain updated by an MIT-rule-like law. Intervention: present drift-transformation sequences in different orders/compositions. Null twin: identical drift transformations and total exposure but morphism labels shuffled so composition is not actually respected by the environment, matching marginal statistics while removing the structure the functor law could exploit.

mechanisms.statement: Two independent online estimators (e.g., a gradient-based and a Kalman-based adaptation law) are treated as two functors from an environment category to a controller category, and a translation map between them is required to be a natural transformation: it must commute with every environment morphism (coordinate change, regime shift). The residual of this naturality square, rather than either estimator's own prediction error, is used as an additional correction signal for both.
mechanisms.what_changes: both adaptation laws are nudged by the naturality-square residual eta_Y∘F(f) - G(f)∘eta_X computed on observed morphisms f
mechanisms.what_persists: the translation components eta_X, accumulated as a cross-estimator dictionary reused in new but related states
mechanisms.what_is_selected: estimator pairs whose translation achieves the lowest average naturality residual over sampled morphisms
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a naturality-consistent estimator pair can be cloned into a fresh agent facing a related environment category
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the translation components eta_X are learned online from morphism-indexed data
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a translation fit on observed morphisms predicts correct estimator-conversion on unobserved morphisms/states
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: naturality-square residual and downstream tracking error compared to a baseline that simply ensemble-averages the two estimators without using morphism structure; the naturality-driven version should generalize the translation to unseen states, the ensemble should not
mechanisms.minimal_world: A pendulum represented in two coordinate systems (angle vs. Cartesian-like features) with morphisms being known coordinate changes at varying operating points; two adaptive estimators track state in each representation. Null twin: same two estimators and same coordinate-change events but morphism identities are randomly relabeled, preserving state statistics while destroying the actual structural correspondence the naturality constraint depends on.

mechanisms.statement: System identification and controller synthesis are modeled as an adjoint pair of functors L (Ident) and R (Synth) between a plant category and a controller category. Online adaptation implements running estimates of the unit and counit natural transformations, and the adaptation error is defined as the failure of the triangle identities, not raw prediction error. Both identification and control parameters are updated jointly to shrink this triangle-identity residual.
mechanisms.what_changes: eta and epsilon (and hence identification/control parameters) are updated by gradient descent on the combined triangle-identity residual plus tracking error
mechanisms.what_persists: the adjoint structure (L, R, eta, epsilon) across episodes, refined rather than reinitialized
mechanisms.what_is_selected: parameter sets minimizing joint residual + tracking error, retained across episodes
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: an established adjoint pair can be instantiated on a new plant instance to bootstrap identification/control jointly
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the unit and counit maps themselves, learned incrementally from tracking data
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: rapid re-adaptation to a new plant using only an updated unit map, without resynthesizing the controller from scratch
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: convergence speed and asymptotic bias of the adjoint-coupled scheme versus a decoupled certainty-equivalence pipeline (identify then separately synthesize) with matched compute
mechanisms.minimal_world: A family of linear plants with unknown scalar gain; identification via recursive least squares, control via pole placement, coupled through the triangle-identity loss. Null twin: identical plants, identical L and R architectures and compute budget, but the triangle-identity coupling term ablated so identification and control adapt independently, matching total gradient steps.

mechanisms.statement: The internal model is maintained as a colimit of local linear patches glued along overlap regions rather than as one global parameter vector. When prediction error on the current patch exceeds threshold, a pushout operation adds a new patch glued to existing ones along shared boundary states, expanding the atlas instead of overwriting it. Old patches remain available and are re-activated when their domain recurs.
mechanisms.what_changes: local patch parameters update by recursive least squares within their domain; the atlas topology changes only via pushout events when residual exceeds threshold
mechanisms.what_persists: previously created patches and their gluing maps, retained indefinitely unless pruned by disuse
mechanisms.what_is_selected: patches with low residual on their domain and glue maps that keep neighboring triangles commuting are kept; inconsistent patches are merged or discarded
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a sub-atlas (patch plus its glue maps) can be forked to seed a model for a related plant sharing that operating regime
mechanisms.what_can_learn: per-patch parameters via RLS; atlas topology via pushout/merge events
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: shared patches reused across tasks/plants that revisit the same operating regime, without retraining
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: performance retention when returning to an old regime after visiting a new one, compared against a single monolithic global adaptive model (plain RLS) which should show catastrophic forgetting of the old regime
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 1D piecewise-linear plant that switches among several regimes over time. Intervention: revisit an earlier regime after a long excursion elsewhere. Null twin: identical regime-switch schedule and total adaptation steps, but the patches are forced to share a single global parameter vector (no gluing/pushout), matching switch statistics while removing compositional memory.

mechanisms.statement: A controller's functional identity is defined by its response profile to a fixed set of canonical probe trajectories (its representable functor Hom(-,C)), not by its raw parameter vector. Two controllers are treated as interchangeable for transfer purposes exactly when their probe-response profiles are naturally isomorphic across probe compositions, even if their underlying parameters differ substantially.
what_exists: probe set (reference signals) with composition structure
mechanisms.what_changes: internal controller parameters adapt online via a standard control law; independently, the probe-response signature is recomputed periodically
mechanisms.what_persists: the compressed probe-response signature, carried forward as the controller's portable identity
mechanisms.what_is_selected: for any transplantation/transfer decision, the controller whose signature is nearest (Yoneda-distance) to a target signature is chosen
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a signature can be reinstantiated in a fresh controller instance by fitting new parameters to reproduce the same probe responses
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the probe-to-response mapping is learned online via active probing
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: swapping one controller implementation for another with matching signature should preserve task performance despite differing parameters
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: task performance after controller-swap-by-signature versus swap-by-raw-parameter-nearest-neighbor, tested on a plant with parameter redundancy (multiple gain vectors giving identical probe behavior)
mechanisms.minimal_world: A linear plant with a redundant/non-identifiable gain parameterization (several distinct gain vectors yield identical closed-loop behavior on the probe set). Null twin: same plant, probes, and redundancy, but controller selection/transfer decisions made by raw parameter-space distance rather than probe-signature distance, matching computational budget while ignoring the representable-functor structure.

mechanisms.statement: Sequential online adaptation across a curriculum of tasks is required to satisfy an associativity law: adapting on A then (B then C) must agree, up to bounded discrepancy, with adapting on (A then B) then C, and with direct adaptation on the composite. A canonicalization operator mu collapses any doubly-adapted controller state onto this single-adaptation manifold, and adaptation laws are shaped to minimize the mu-discrepancy.
what_exists: single-shot reference adaptation state for composite tasks
mechanisms.what_changes: after every pair of successive adaptations, mu re-projects the stacked state toward the canonical single-adaptation state; adaptation-law parameters are tuned to shrink this discrepancy over time
mechanisms.what_persists: the canonical single-adaptation manifold used as the comparison target across all curricula
mechanisms.what_is_selected: adaptation laws/lineages with low associativity-violation error are retained; high-drift lineages are pruned
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a canonicalized post-mu controller state can seed a new training lineage
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the mu operator's parameters, learned to minimize discrepancy between staged and composite adaptation
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: final competence that is invariant to the order in which a fixed task set was presented
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: variance of final task performance across permutations of a fixed task curriculum for the mu-constrained scheme versus a plain sequential adaptive controller with matched total gradient steps
mechanisms.minimal_world: A sequence of drifting linear plants (tasks A, B, C) presented in different orders. Null twin: identical task set, total exposure time, and gradient budget, but mu replaced by the identity map (no canonicalization step), matching compute while removing the associativity-shaping constraint.

mechanisms.statement: Two adaptive controllers track the same underlying plant through different reference models; instead of each minimizing only its own tracking error, adaptation is driven additionally by the pullback mismatch: the disagreement between their state estimates once mapped into a shared comparison space via fixed projection maps. This mismatch term couples the two adaptation laws, producing consensus dynamics absent from independently tuned controllers.
what_exists: fixed projection maps p1, p2 into a comparison space
mechanisms.what_changes: each controller's adaptation law updates on its own tracking error plus the term p1(x1)-p2(x2) computed at each step
mechanisms.what_persists: the fixed comparison-space projections across the run
mechanisms.what_is_selected: controller pairs that reduce pullback mismatch fastest are retained/propagated in an ensemble setting
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a converged pair can spawn a merged controller whose parameters are the pullback (limit) of the two
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the projection maps themselves, if adapted slowly when persistent mismatch remains despite individual convergence
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the merged/limit controller generalizes more robustly to new plant instances than either individual controller alone
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: convergence speed and noise robustness of the pullback-coupled pair versus a post-hoc simple average of two independently adapted controllers given identical sensor information
mechanisms.minimal_world: Two noisy sensors of the same 1D linear plant expressed in different reference-model units, each driving its own adaptive controller. Null twin: identical sensors, plant, and noise, but each controller's adaptation uses only its own tracking error with no cross pullback term, matching total information available while removing the coupling.

mechanisms.statement: Operating regimes form a category whose morphisms are known regime-transitions; controller-gain assignment across regimes is required to be natural with respect to this category, meaning the gain after a transition must equal the transition's induced action on the gain before it. Adaptation explicitly minimizes the commutator norm of this naturality square across observed transitions, yielding a gain schedule that predicts gains for unseen regimes via the transition action rather than per-regime fitting.
mechanisms.what_changes: at each observed transition, T* and/or the gain assignment are updated to shrink ||g(T(r)) - T*(g(r))||
mechanisms.what_persists: the transition-action map T*, reused for regimes never directly visited
mechanisms.what_is_selected: gain schedules/T* candidates with the smallest transient ('bump') at observed transitions
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: T* can be exported to a new plant instance whose regime category is structurally analogous
mechanisms.what_can_learn: T* is estimated online purely from observed transition data
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: zero-shot prediction of the correct gain for a never-visited regime via T*, tested against nearest-neighbor interpolation over regime features
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: transient magnitude at regime switches and accuracy of predicted gain for a held-out regime, comparing the naturality-constrained scheduler to independently-tuned per-regime gains and to feature-based interpolation
mechanisms.minimal_world: A plant with five discrete operating regimes connected by a known transition graph, with some edges never traversed during training. Null twin: same regimes and marginal visitation frequencies but transitions relabeled at random (no consistent graph action), removing the morphism structure T* could exploit while matching regime frequency statistics.

mechanisms.statement: Rather than maintaining independent parameters for each context, adaptation maintains a single 'end' object: the unique parameter choice compatible with wedge maps from all contexts in an indexing category. Per-context deviations are pulled toward this shared end at a rate proportional to their wedge-consistency violation, forcing a low-dimensional bottleneck that captures only cross-context-shared structure.
what_exists: wedge maps from contexts to shared end
mechanisms.what_changes: the end estimate updates online whenever new context data violates existing wedge consistency; per-context parameters relax toward the end weighted by consistency-violation magnitude
mechanisms.what_persists: the end estimate itself, a compressed cross-context summary far smaller than the sum of per-context parameters
mechanisms.what_is_selected: the end candidate minimizing total wedge-violation across all contexts (the universal-property winner)
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the end parameter alone can be handed to a fresh controller for a new related context
mechanisms.what_can_learn: online refinement of the end as new contexts stream in, enabling few-shot competence
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: held-out-context performance using only the shared end, compared to per-context-fit controllers with matched total parameter budget
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: sample-efficiency curve on a novel context for the end-based bottleneck versus a baseline sharing the same parameter budget but computed as a plain arithmetic mean across contexts (which does not satisfy wedge consistency)
mechanisms.minimal_world: A family of linear plants sharing a hidden common structural component (e.g., identical B matrix, varying A) organized as a small diagram/category. Null twin: identical plant family and parameter budget, but the shared parameter is computed as a simple average of per-context fits rather than an end satisfying all wedge maps, matching compute while breaking the universal property.

mechanisms.statement: Continuous online adaptation is periodically interrupted by an idempotent retraction: the current controller/model state is projected through a fixed reflector R onto a well-formed subcategory (e.g., stable, minimal-realization models), satisfying R(R(x))=R(x). This discrete snap-back corrects accumulated drift or ill-formed artifacts from continuous gradient adaptation in a way that plain continuous regularization cannot guarantee.
mechanisms.what_changes: standard continuous adaptation proceeds between retraction events; at scheduled intervals or on validity-check failure, R is applied once, snapping the state into the well-formed subcategory
mechanisms.what_persists: well-formedness (e.g., stability, minimality) of the state immediately after any retraction event, by construction
mechanisms.what_is_selected: trajectories through parameter space that remain within or return promptly to the well-formed subcategory are retained; those diverging between retractions are flagged/discarded
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a freshly retracted, well-formed controller state can be safely cloned or deployed, since guaranteed properties hold
mechanisms.what_can_learn: optionally, the reflector R itself can be slowly meta-learned to better preserve task performance while enforcing well-formedness
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: retracted states transfer safely to deployment or other agents; unretracted states carry no such guarantee
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: incidence of instability/divergence episodes and long-run performance variance for periodic idempotent retraction versus continuous L2 shrinkage regularization matched in average parameter-correction magnitude
mechanisms.minimal_world: An adaptive pole-placement controller for a plant with slowly drifting parameters, where naive recursive least-squares updates occasionally produce unstable closed-loop gains. Null twin: identical drift and identical average magnitude of parameter correction, but correction is applied as continuous weight decay rather than discrete idempotent projection onto the stable-gain set, matching the nuisance statistic of 'average shrinkage' while lacking the idempotent well-formed-subcategory guarantee.
