mechanisms.statement: Each unit in a layered network maintains an activation state that is iteratively adjusted at inference time to minimize precision-weighted prediction error passed down from higher layers and up from lower layers, prior to any weight change. Weights then change slowly via a local Hebbian-like rule proportional to the settled error times presynaptic activity, so representation and parameter learning are two different timescales of the same error-minimization law.
mechanisms.what_changes: At each timestep, activation_i <- activation_i - eta * (precision_i * error_from_above - precision_i-1 * error_from_below); after settling, weight_ij <- weight_ij + alpha * precision_i * error_i * activation_j.
mechanisms.what_persists: The generative weight matrices and precision estimates persist across trials, encoding the learned model of environmental causes.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Weight configurations that yield lower steady-state prediction error across the training distribution are implicitly favored by the gradient-like update.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: In a population variant, weight sets can be copied wholesale into new agent instances.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The statistical/causal structure generating the sensory stream, encoded hierarchically.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Learned generative weights transfer to novel inputs sharing the same underlying causes but different noise or nuisance variation.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Settling dynamics show iterative error suppression that propagates from low to high layers over multiple timesteps within a single input, and lesioning feedback (top-down) connections should selectively slow or destabilize settling; a feedforward-only regression network matched in parameter count shows no such iterative settling curve or feedback-lesion sensitivity.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 3-layer toy world generates 1-D signals from a small set of hidden causes with additive noise; the mechanism network infers causes via iterative settling and updates weights from settled errors. Intervention: lesion the feedback (error-down) pathway after training and measure settling-time and error curves. Null twin: an equivalent feedforward network trained by ordinary backprop on the same generative data, matched in parameter count and final loss, which by construction has no iterative settling dynamics to lesion, distinguishing the mechanism via the settling-curve/feedback-lesion signature rather than final accuracy.

mechanisms.statement: The environment's observations are generated by composing a small fixed set of reusable primitive functions in novel combinations each episode, so structure recurs across episodes even though surface sequences never repeat exactly. This rule creates a standing pressure for any learner to discover and reuse primitives rather than memorize whole episodes.
what_exists: per-episode composition tree drawn from the grammar
observed sequence produced by executing the composition
mechanisms.what_changes: Each episode samples a new composition (tree over primitives) and renders it into an observation sequence; the primitive set itself is fixed across episodes.
mechanisms.what_persists: The primitive set and their combination rules persist unchanged across all episodes; only the composition varies.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Agent representations/policies that isolate reusable primitives and reuse them across compositions perform better and are favored by any performance-based training signal.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Primitives can be recombined combinatorially to generate unboundedly many novel compositions from the same finite basis.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: An agent can learn to segment observations into primitive-aligned units and predict/act using compositional reuse.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A representation of primitives learned on one subset of compositions transfers zero-shot to unseen compositions built from the same primitives.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Held-out performance on novel compositions should scale with the number of shared primitives with training compositions and remain well above chance; a memorizing learner (null) shows near-chance performance on any composition not seen verbatim, even though both learners can match training-set performance identically.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A gridworld where objects are rendered by composing 4 primitive shape/motion functions in random order/combination each episode; train on a subset of compositions, test on held-out novel compositions using the same primitives. Intervention: swap which primitives are shown together during training vs testing to force compositional generalization. Null twin: an environment where each episode's rendering function is drawn independently at random (no shared primitive basis) but matched in per-episode observation statistics (same marginal distributions), so surface-level statistics match but there is no reusable substructure to exploit.

mechanisms.statement: A router module observes each input and selects exactly one of several expert modules to process it (hard, discrete routing); only the selected expert's parameters are updated on that trial, while the router's gating weights are updated by the task loss with respect to the routing decision. This creates architectural pressure toward specialization: each expert experiences a non-random subset of the input distribution.
what_exists: N expert modules with independent parameters
per-trial input and hard gate decision
mechanisms.what_changes: argmax/softmax-sampled gate selects expert e for input x; expert_e parameters updated by gradient of task loss on x; router parameters updated by gradient of task loss with respect to gate probabilities (e.g. via a straight-through or REINFORCE estimator).
mechanisms.what_persists: Expert parameter sets persist across trials and gradually specialize; router weights persist, encoding the input-to-expert partition.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Experts that reduce loss for the input cluster routed to them continue to receive that cluster (a self-reinforcing selection loop between router and experts).
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: An overloaded expert can be duplicated into two experts that subsequently diverge under continued routing (optional reproduction operator).
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The router learns an implicit partition of input space; each expert learns a local function specialized to its partition.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A single frozen expert can be transplanted into a new router facing a new task distribution that shares a subpopulation with the old expert's niche, and should immediately perform well on that subpopulation without retraining.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Usage statistics should be bimodal/sparse (few experts active per input, consistent expert-to-subpopulation mapping across trials), and ablating a single expert should selectively impair performance only on its niche inputs; a dense monolithic network matched in total parameters shows no such selective-ablation profile because damage is distributed roughly proportional to overall capacity used, not niche-specific.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A classification task with inputs drawn from K clearly separable subpopulations (e.g. K clusters in 2D) routed through 4 experts. Intervention: after training, zero out one expert's parameters and measure accuracy per subpopulation. Null twin: a single dense network with matched total parameter count trained on the identical data, then equivalently ablate a matched fraction of its parameters (e.g. a random or magnitude-based subset) and compare the resulting per-subpopulation damage pattern, which should be diffuse rather than niche-localized.

mechanisms.statement: Training jointly minimizes data-fit loss and an explicit description-length / complexity cost on the model's parameters, with the complexity weight increased over training, so the model is pressured toward the simplest representation still consistent with the data (an explicit minimum-description-length pressure rather than fit-only optimization). This pressure operates as a scheduled meta-parameter distinct from ordinary regularization strength tuned for generalization.
what_exists: explicit complexity/code-length cost C(theta) (e.g. bits needed to specify theta at given precision)
mechanisms.what_changes: theta <- theta - eta * grad(D(theta) + lambda(t) * C(theta)); lambda(t) increases according to a fixed schedule, progressively pruning/quantizing less-useful parameters.
mechanisms.what_persists: The minimal sufficient parameter subset that survives increasing lambda persists as the compressed model.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Parameter configurations with the best fit-per-bit ratio at each lambda level are retained; redundant/low-utility parameters are pruned.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Compressed sub-modules can be extracted and reused/duplicated as building blocks in a larger composed model.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: Increasingly compressed, generalization-favoring representations as compression pressure ramps up.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A compressed representation should transfer to a novel low-data task better than an uncompressed model matched in training-loss, because it has discarded overfit-specific parameters.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: As lambda increases, held-out generalization should improve (or degrade more slowly) up to a critical compression level, then collapse sharply past a description-length threshold — a non-monotonic/threshold generalization-vs-compression curve absent in a fit-only model (lambda=0 fixed) matched in final training loss, which shows a flat or monotonically worsening generalization curve as capacity is externally reduced without the joint fit/complexity optimization.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A small regression task with a true low-complexity generator plus noise; train models under a schedule of increasing lambda vs a fixed lambda=0 control matched at each checkpoint for training loss via early stopping. Intervention: sweep lambda schedules and measure held-out loss and effective description length (e.g. number of non-negligible weights) at each checkpoint. Null twin: an unregularized model trained to the same training loss trajectory via early stopping alone (no explicit complexity term), matched in training-loss curve but with no code-length pressure, which should show no corresponding non-monotonic generalization-vs-complexity relationship.

mechanisms.statement: Feature-encoding units carry both an amplitude (feature intensity) and a phase (grouping tag); units representing features that belong to the same object become phase-coupled via a Kuramoto-like coupling rule, so that binding information is carried independently of feature content. Downstream readout uses relative phase, not amplitude, to determine which features belong together.
what_exists: oscillatory units with amplitude a_i and phase theta_i
a coupling weight matrix K_ij learned from task feedback
a downstream relational readout comparing phase differences
mechanisms.what_changes: theta_i <- theta_i + dt * sum_j K_ij * sin(theta_j - theta_i) (phase dynamics); K_ij updated by gradient of a downstream relational task loss (e.g. correct grouping/query answer) with respect to coupling weights.
mechanisms.what_persists: The coupling matrix K persists across trials, encoding which feature-pairs tend to co-occur as parts of the same object.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Coupling configurations that produce phase clusters matching ground-truth object boundaries are reinforced by task reward/loss.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Coupling matrices can be copied into a new agent's oscillator population as a prior.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: Which feature co-occurrences imply common object membership, learned purely from downstream binding-task error.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Learned binding rules generalize to novel objects composed of familiar features in new combinations, tested via correct grouping on unseen composite stimuli.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Downstream task accuracy should collapse when phases are experimentally scrambled while amplitudes are held fixed, but remain intact when amplitudes are scrambled and phase relations preserved; a rate/amplitude-only encoding model (null) is insensitive to phase scrambling by construction and instead degrades only under amplitude scrambling — the double-dissociation is the key signature.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A synthetic scene with multiple objects, each defined by 2-3 co-occurring features (color, shape, position) rendered as unit activations; task is to answer relational queries (e.g. 'what shape is the red object'). Intervention: after training, independently scramble phase-only vs amplitude-only across units and measure query accuracy in each condition. Null twin: a matched-capacity model that encodes objects purely via amplitude/rate patterns with no separate phase variable (binding done implicitly via a learned combined amplitude code), tested under the same two scrambling interventions, which should show no phase-specific vulnerability since it has no phase variable to scramble in the first place (scrambling a dummy phase variable added post-hoc has no effect on its output).

mechanisms.statement: A fast, one-shot Hebbian associative matrix stores each new experience immediately and decays quickly, while a slow network is trained only via periodic replay of buffered experiences and changes little per step. New experiences are thus available for immediate recall via the fast store, and only become part of the slow store's generalizable statistics after repeated interleaved replay.
what_exists: replay buffer of stored (input,target) patterns with priority tags
mechanisms.what_changes: On each new experience (x,y): W_fast <- W_fast + eta_fast * outer(y,x) (one-shot); pattern added to buffer with priority (e.g. surprise/reward); W_fast decays each step: W_fast <- (1-delta)*W_fast; periodically, batches sampled from buffer are used for small gradient updates to W_slow.
mechanisms.what_persists: Statistical regularities embedded in W_slow persist indefinitely; individual episodic traces in W_fast persist only transiently.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Buffer sampling priority selects which experiences get replayed and thus which patterns are consolidated into W_slow.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: The consolidated W_slow can be copied wholesale into a new agent instance as a pretrained initialization.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: Both immediate one-shot recall (fast store) and slow cross-episode generalization (slow store).
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: W_slow generalizes to novel instances of previously-seen categories; W_fast supports recall of the exact specific episode but does not generalize — this dissociation is directly testable.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: After learning many new items sequentially, retention of early items measured via the slow store should remain high (protected by interleaved replay) while a single-weight-matrix online learner without a fast/slow split and without replay (null, matched in total parameter count and per-step update cost) shows sharp catastrophic forgetting of early items as new ones are learned.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A sequence of pattern-association tasks (e.g. paired associates) presented one at a time; the dual-store model learns each via W_fast immediately and consolidates via periodic replay into W_slow. Intervention: measure recall accuracy on early-learned pairs after many subsequent pairs, with and without replay enabled. Null twin: a single associative matrix updated online on each new pair with no replay and no fast/slow split, matched in total learnable parameters and per-example update magnitude, tested identically for retention of early pairs.

mechanisms.what_persists: Duplicated substructures persist as redundant backups across generations unless divergence and selection repurpose one copy into a distinct specialized sub-function.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Graphs with higher task fitness reproduce more; among duplicate pairs, whichever divergent trajectory improves fitness (via specialization or robustness) is retained by selection.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: Whole graphs reproduce with mutation into the next generation; subgraphs 'reproduce' internally via the duplication step itself.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: Population-level structural learning across generations (which sub-functions are useful is discovered evolutionarily, not within a single lifetime).
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: A duplicated-and-diverged module that specialized into a new sub-function can be excised and transplanted into a different graph solving a related task, tested for immediate functional contribution without further tuning.

The null twin is identical except k=n (no truncation), matching all update equations and data statistics but removing compression, so it shows no forced low-dimensional structure and no transfer advantage.

mechanisms.statement: States are represented by their orbit under a specified symmetry group G, computed via a group-averaged or canonicalized invariant feature map, so the representation factors through the quotient space X/G. Inputs related by any g in G collapse to an identical representation. This produces automatic generalization to unseen group transformations without additional training examples covering them.
what_exists: a group G acting on X
an invariant map phi(x) (average or canonicalization over G)
mechanisms.what_changes: raw x is replaced by phi(x) before downstream processing; candidate groups/generators can be swapped and tested
mechanisms.what_persists: phi(x) is constant under x -> g.x for all g in G
mechanisms.what_is_selected: the candidate group whose induced phi minimizes downstream prediction error
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the canonicalization function can be copied to new domains sharing the same symmetry
mechanisms.what_can_learn: which subgroup/generators actually leave the label invariant, via consistency testing
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: predictors trained on phi(x) transfer zero-shot to all g.x
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: zero-shot accuracy on group-transformed test inputs equals in-distribution accuracy for the invariant representation, while a non-equivariant representation of matched capacity shows a large accuracy drop under the same transformations
mechanisms.minimal_world: Small grid images of shapes where label=shape identity and nuisance=90-degree rotation (G=cyclic rotation group). Train only on 0-degree orientation using phi(x)=average over the 4 rotations; test on unseen 90/180/270-degree rotations. The null twin uses raw pixel features of matched dimensionality and identical training but no group-averaging, then is tested identically.

mechanisms.statement: A recurrent map f_theta is built to be a contraction (Lipschitz constant L<1), so by the Banach fixed-point theorem iteration converges from any starting point in its basin to a unique attractor. Storing a pattern means parameterizing theta so a fixed point sits there; recall is iterating f_theta from a noisy cue until convergence. Multiple non-overlapping basins give discrete, content-addressable memories from pure contraction geometry.
what_exists: enforced contraction constant L<1 (e.g., via spectral normalization)
mechanisms.what_changes: theta is updated when storing a new pattern; s updates as s_{t+1}=f_theta(s_t) during recall
mechanisms.what_persists: the fixed point s*=f_theta(s*) as long as theta is unchanged
mechanisms.what_is_selected: patterns whose basins remain non-overlapping (sufficient fixed-point separation relative to L) are retained
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a stored attractor's theta can be copied into another contraction-map instance
mechanisms.what_can_learn: theta is learned via gradient or Hebbian-like rule to place a fixed point at a target pattern
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the same contraction operator transfers to storing new pattern sets
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: recall distance-to-attractor decreases geometrically with iteration count matching ||s_t-s*||<=L^t||s_0-s*||; a null twin with L>=1 diverges or wanders instead of showing guaranteed geometric convergence
mechanisms.minimal_world: 5 patterns stored as fixed points of contraction maps sharing one recurrent layer; corrupt cues with varying flip-noise and measure convergence trajectories/basin boundaries. The null twin uses identical architecture and stored patterns but weights rescaled so spectral radius exceeds 1, matching parameter count but lacking the contraction guarantee.

mechanisms.statement: Internal representations are encoded with structured redundancy via a linear parity-check code, and corrupted values are corrected by iterative message passing over the constraint (Tanner) graph. This lets the system exactly recover a clean state from noisy readouts, as long as noise stays under the code's correction radius, without storing the clean state directly.
mechanisms.what_changes: iterative belief updates at variable and check nodes converge to a corrected estimate c_hat
mechanisms.what_persists: the code structure (G,H) across arbitrarily many different messages
mechanisms.what_is_selected: codes whose correction radius best matches the empirical noise level, by comparing post-decode error rate
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the (G,H) scaffold can be reused to encode new messages
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the redundancy structure H can be adapted to match the actual noise channel statistics
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a decoder tuned for one noise regime transfers correction capability to new messages under similar noise
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: post-decoding error rate stays near zero below a sharp corruption-rate threshold then fails catastrophically above it, unlike a null twin using matched-redundancy repetition-averaging which degrades gradually with a strictly worse threshold at the same code rate
mechanisms.minimal_world: 4-bit messages sent through a binary symmetric channel with tunable flip probability p, encoded via a (7,4) Hamming-style code and decoded by message passing; sweep p and measure error rate vs. a null twin sending the same 4 bits via triple-repetition of some bits (matched codeword length/rate) with no structured parity/message-passing.

mechanisms.statement: Among hypotheses fitting data equally well, the system is pressured by an explicit two-part code-length score (model description length plus data-given-model length) to prefer the shortest total encoding. This converts generalization into optimizing code length rather than raw fit, penalizing memorization.
mechanisms.what_changes: a search process proposes hypotheses and updates the running best h* = argmin L(h)+L(D|h) as data accumulates
mechanisms.what_persists: h* persists until a hypothesis with strictly lower total code length is found
mechanisms.what_is_selected: hypotheses minimizing simplicity-weighted total description length
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: h* can be exported as a compact generator to predict new data
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the encoding scheme's own cost function can be recalibrated as data reveals the true regularity class
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a short hypothesis learned on one dataset predicts well on new data from the same source, unlike an overfit long hypothesis
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: held-out prediction error is strictly lower for the MDL-selected hypothesis than a maximum-likelihood-only hypothesis at matched training error, especially at small training sizes, with the gap shrinking as data grows
mechanisms.minimal_world: Sequences generated by a short finite-state automaton plus noise; the learner searches automata of varying size, scoring by MDL, vs. a null twin scoring purely by training-data fit with an identical search procedure and hypothesis space; compare held-out next-symbol accuracy across training-prefix lengths.

mechanisms.statement: Among a population of predictive models, selection favors the one with the lowest recent average surprisal (-log p(observation)), a survival-of-the-least-surprised rule where low scorers are culled and replaced by mutated copies of high scorers. This creates a competitive predictor market where a proper scoring rule directly determines persistence and propagation.
what_exists: running score S_i (moving average negative log-likelihood)
mechanisms.what_changes: each model does local parameter updates between selection events; the population is periodically reweighted/culled by S_i
mechanisms.what_persists: models with sustained low surprisal persist across resampling steps
mechanisms.what_is_selected: models with lowest cumulative negative log-likelihood on recent data
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: high-scoring models are copied with mutation to replace low scorers
mechanisms.what_can_learn: individual models perform local learning (e.g., gradient) between selection events
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a surviving model's parameters transfer to descendants and to new environments with similar statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: population-average surprisal decreases faster than any single model's isolated learning curve, and adapts faster to regime shifts, than a null twin with identical local learning but no selection/replacement (parallel independent learners)
mechanisms.minimal_world: Data generated by two Markov chains that switch abruptly at random times; run 20 models with local learning plus selection-and-mutation (window 50), vs. a null twin with the same 20 models and learning rule but no culling; measure time-to-adapt after each regime switch.

mechanisms.statement: A system repeatedly applies a fixed local coarse-graining operator to its own representation, producing a tower of representations at increasing scales that keep only slow/relevant variables. Structure invariant under this flow (an RG fixed point) becomes the emergent high-level representation, so hierarchy arises from repeated application of one simple rule rather than a designed architecture.
what_exists: fine-grained state field x on a lattice/graph
mechanisms.what_changes: the representation is replaced by its coarse-grained image at each step; parameters of R may be tuned to preserve target statistics across the transform
mechanisms.what_persists: features that are fixed points of R (self-similar structure) survive across levels
mechanisms.what_is_selected: coarse-graining rules maximizing retained predictive information about a downstream label at each step
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the same tuned operator R is reapplied identically at every level
mechanisms.what_can_learn: parameters of R are learned to preserve label-relevant statistics under repeated coarse-graining
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: coarse representations learned on one fine-grained instantiation transfer to systems with different fine details but matching coarse statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: mutual information with the label decays much more slowly across levels than with nuisance details, giving a plateau at the true structural scale; a null twin coarse-graining via randomly permuted block assignment (matched compression ratio) shows label- and nuisance-information decaying at the same rate with no plateau
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 1D/2D Ising-like lattice whose label is the sign of large-scale magnetization plus small-scale random noise spins; apply repeated block-decimation and measure mutual information with label vs. level, compared to a null twin using randomly permuted (scrambled-adjacency) block grouping with matched block size and arithmetic.

mechanisms.statement: A recurrent network's coupling gain is tuned so its maximal Lyapunov exponent sits near zero, the boundary between ordered and chaotic dynamics. At this critical point the system maximizes its capacity to separate distinct input histories into distinguishable trajectories while retaining long transient memory, without collapsing inputs together or amplifying noise unboundedly.
what_exists: coupled nonlinear units with state s_t
coupling matrix W scaled by gain g
mechanisms.what_changes: g is adjusted by a slow homeostatic rule based on measured local Lyapunov exponent from perturbed trajectory pairs
mechanisms.what_persists: the near-critical operating point (lambda_max ~ 0) is continually restored after input statistics change
mechanisms.what_is_selected: gain values keeping lambda_max within a narrow band around zero
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the tuned coupling matrix/scaling rule can be copied into new instances with similar input statistics
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a linear readout trained on the fixed recurrent trajectories learns task-specific projections
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the near-critical operating point and its separation capacity transfer to different but statistically similar input ensembles
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: task performance vs. gain g forms a sharp inverted-U peaking at the empirically measured critical g (lambda_max crossing zero); a null twin homeostatically targeting fixed activity variance/mean instead of Lyapunov exponent shows only a smooth monotonic dependence with no sharp peak at that location
mechanisms.minimal_world: A small recurrent tanh network with random fixed connectivity scaled by gain g, driven by random binary pulses; estimate lambda_max via twin-trajectory divergence, sweep g, and measure a linear readout's delayed-XOR memory accuracy vs. g, compared to a null twin using variance-homeostasis tuning with identical architecture and readout training.

mechanisms.statement: A family of maps between representations at different domains is constrained to commute with a fixed set of structural operations (a naturality square: F(g(x)) = g'(F(x))). This categorical constraint forces learned maps to respect compositional structure rather than fit arbitrary pointwise correlations, guaranteeing generalization to any element reachable by composing the structural maps.
what_exists: domains X, Y each with structural operations g in X, g' in Y
mechanisms.what_changes: F's parameters are updated to jointly minimize pointwise prediction error and naturality-violation ||F(g(x)) - g'(F(x))|| averaged over sampled g, x
mechanisms.what_persists: once naturality-violation reaches zero it persists under further training as an algebraic identity, not a statistical regularity
mechanisms.what_is_selected: among F's fitting training data equally, those with lowest naturality-violation
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: F can be composed with itself or other natural maps to construct new natural transformations by construction
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the correspondence g<->g' itself can be searched for if not given
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: F trained on a small orbit of X generalizes exactly to the entire orbit reachable by composing g's, even unseen compositions
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: test error on elements reachable only by unseen compositions of g stays near zero for the naturality-constrained F, while a null twin with identical data/architecture/pointwise loss but no naturality penalty shows error growing with the number of compositional steps away from training examples
mechanisms.minimal_world: X = symbol sequences with shift operation g; Y = their numeric encodings with corresponding shift g'. Train F on unshifted and once-shifted examples; test on 2,3,4-times-shifted sequences. The constrained learner adds a naturality loss enforcing F(shift(x))=shift'(F(x)); the null twin uses identical architecture, data, and optimizer with only the pointwise reconstruction loss.

mechanisms.statement: The system has a primitive enabling a procedure to refer to and apply itself (a fixed-point/Y-combinator construction: R(f) = f(R(f))), letting a finite set of base rules generate unbounded-depth recursive procedures. This is what allows a fixed rule-set to solve problem instances of arbitrarily large size without adding new rules per size.
what_exists: a small set of base combinators/functions
an environment with first-class functions supporting self-application
problem instances of varying size n
mechanisms.what_changes: given a base case and recursive case, the fixed-point construction assembles one recursive procedure that is reused, unmodified, across all n
mechanisms.what_persists: the single derived recursive procedure persists unchanged and is reused across all n
mechanisms.what_is_selected: candidate (base-case, recursive-case) bodies whose fixed-point closure solves training instances across multiple sizes are retained over non-recursive size-specific bodies
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the recursive procedure calls/reproduces itself at run time and can be reused as a subroutine in larger recursive programs
mechanisms.what_can_learn: only the base-case and recursive-case sub-functions need to be searched/learned; the recursion scaffold is fixed
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a recursive procedure induced from small instances transfers zero-shot to arbitrarily larger n, unlike a non-recursive lookup/unrolled table
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: accuracy vs. instance size n stays flat for the recursion-based solver trained only on small n, while a null twin with equal parameter count learning a size-unrolled fixed-depth mapping collapses in accuracy as n grows beyond the training range
mechanisms.minimal_world: List-processing tasks (sum, reverse) with training data limited to lists of length 1-3; the recursion solver is given a self-application operator plus head/tail/cons primitives and induces base+recursive definitions via search. The null twin has identical primitives, search budget, and training data but only fixed-depth composition (no self-application), matching parameter budget. Test both on lengths 3 through 20.

mechanisms.statement: The control parameter that sets a trophic module's qualitative regime (fixed point, limit cycle, chaos) is not an externally imposed constant but is itself the instantaneous ecosystem energy input rate propagated through conversion efficiencies. As flux crosses thresholds implied by the module's Jacobian, eigenvalues cross the unit circle and true bifurcations occur, so resource pulses are bifurcation forcings rather than mere state perturbations.
mechanisms.what_changes: x_i(t+1)=x_i(t)+x_i(t)[r_i(E(t))-sum_j a_ij x_j(t)]; E(t+1)=E(t)+input(t)-uptake(t); r_i(E) continuously reshapes the community Jacobian, crossing bifurcation thresholds at specific E* values.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: none; this is a pure forced dynamical law, not a selection process.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: populations via standard density-dependent growth.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: nothing adapts; the mechanism is purely dynamical.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the bifurcation-threshold structure should transfer across different network topologies sharing the same E(t) schedule.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the largest local Lyapunov exponent should show a sharp, theory-predicted discontinuity precisely at E* values derived from linearization, not a smooth drift.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 3-node chain (basal resource, herbivore, predator) with a stepwise input(t) schedule; intervention manipulates input(t) directly while holding A fixed, recording Lyapunov exponent and regime before/after threshold. Null twin: identical equations but r_i held constant while growth rate receives injected noise matched in variance/autocorrelation to the real E(t) trace; the null should show gradual, unthresholded changes in dynamics uncorrelated with the theoretical E* values.

mechanisms.statement: Removing or adding a single node changes not just fixed-point locations but the volume and boundary geometry of the basins of attraction in a multistable community; a species' 'keystone-ness' is defined as the derivative of basin-volume partition with respect to its removal, independent of its biomass or degree.
mechanisms.what_changes: removing row/column i of A changes the vector field f(x;A); Monte Carlo sampling of initial conditions recomputes the fraction converging to each attractor before vs after removal.
mechanisms.what_persists: the identity of surviving attractors, even as their basin volumes shift.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none directly; this is a structural rule, not a selection process.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: species reproduce logistically within f(x;A).
mechanisms.what_can_learn: not applicable to this mechanism alone.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: keystone rank should be invariant to uniform rescaling of all edge weights, testable directly.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: a low-biomass, low-degree species can produce disproportionate basin reorganization (large total-variation distance in basin partition), which a biomass/degree-based ranking cannot predict.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 4-species Lotka-Volterra system engineered with two coexisting stable attractors; intervention removes each species and resamples 10,000 initial conditions to measure basin-fraction shifts. Null twin: replace the removed species with a passive constant biomass offset added to other species' growth terms (matching total redistributed biomass) but without its nonlinear coupling terms; basin volumes should not shift in the null.

mechanisms.statement: A slow abiotic state variable (nutrient/detritus pool) integrates the history of fast species dynamics and thereby determines which successional trajectory is realized from a disturbance; identical instantaneous abundance vectors can yield different futures depending on this slow variable's value, producing genuine hysteresis.
mechanisms.what_changes: x_{t+1}=g(x,D); D_{t+1}=D_t+epsilon*(mortality inputs - decay*D_t), with D updating far slower than x.
mechanisms.what_persists: D persists across disturbance events even when x is reset near zero.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none directly in this mechanism.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: species reproduce; D only accumulates/decays.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the ecosystem trajectory encodes integrated disturbance history in D, biasing future successional pathway.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: D-encoded legacy can transfer across patches via diffusion, testable by translocating soil/D values.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: identical resets of x(0) but different D(0) histories should yield divergent long-run community attractors correlated with D(0); a memoryless system predicts convergence regardless of D(0).
mechanisms.minimal_world: One patch, 3 species, one nutrient pool D; disturbance resets x to near-zero at two times with different pre-existing D. Null twin: replace slow D accumulation with instantaneous equilibration D=D_eq(x(t)) at every step (matched in steady-state mean/variance) — successional outcome should be history-independent in the null.

mechanisms.statement: When interaction strengths are heritable and mutable, and species with locally chaotic (large positive Lyapunov exponent) trajectories go extinct more often, selection over generations biases surviving networks toward negative local Lyapunov exponents — stability becomes an emergent selected property rather than an assumed equilibrium.
what_exists: per-lineage local Lyapunov exponent lambda_i from trailing Jacobian products
mechanisms.what_changes: A mutates via Gaussian perturbation on reproduction; extinction probability for species i increases with lambda_i; survivors reproduce with mutated edge-weight copies into colonizing species.
mechanisms.what_persists: heritable edge-weight genome passed with modification across lineages.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: interaction-weight genotypes yielding low local Lyapunov exponent under prevailing energy flux.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: species demographically, and lineages genealogically via edge-weight inheritance to colonizers.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the network-level mean lambda drifts downward over generations, a population-level stability learning process.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: stabilized motifs (negative feedback loops) discovered under selection should retain low lambda when transplanted into fresh random networks.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: community-mean lambda should drift systematically downward under Lyapunov-correlated extinction but not under Lyapunov-blind extinction at matched extinction rate.
mechanisms.minimal_world: 6-10 species with mutable pairwise coefficients under logistic dynamics; extinction probability increases with estimated lambda_i. Null twin: identical mutation operator and extinction rate, but extinction chosen uniformly among low-abundance species irrespective of lambda (matched extinction frequency/abundance distribution); no systematic lambda drift should occur in the null.

mechanisms.statement: Each trophic transfer acts as a nonlinear low-pass filter of prey fluctuations via saturating functional response and conversion-efficiency loss, so successive trophic levels see progressively information-reduced, low-frequency-biased versions of basal fluctuations; chain length sets an intrinsic bandwidth limit on how much environmental variability reaches apex levels.
what_exists: saturating Holling type-II functional response h
mechanisms.what_changes: x_k(t+1)=x_k(t)+x_k(t)[c*h(x_{k-1}(t))-m_k]; mutual information I(s;x_k) is computed per frequency band via spectral decomposition.
mechanisms.what_persists: chain topology (fixed number of trophic levels) across the run.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none directly here; chain length could be selected for in an evolutionary extension.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: populations reproduce logistically at each level.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: not intrinsic, but sets an upper bound on any downstream tracker's achievable information about basal fluctuations.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the bandwidth-limiting property should be invariant to rescaling h while preserving saturation shape.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: mutual information loss should be concentrated in high-frequency bands (low-pass signature) rather than uniform across frequencies.
mechanisms.minimal_world: Linear 4-level food chain driven by stochastic basal input s(t); intervention varies the saturation half-constant at each link, measuring coherence spectrum between s and x_4. Null twin: replace the saturating response with a linear-gain response plus i.i.d. multiplicative noise tuned to match total variance reduction in x_4; the null predicts uniform, not frequency-selective, information loss.

mechanisms.statement: Interaction-strength mutations are gated by locally experienced energy flux: lineages in energy deficit mutate with larger/directed steps toward new or stronger resource edges, while lineages in surplus mutate conservatively, producing a state-dependent variation-generation process coupled dynamically to ecosystem energy flow rather than an unconditional mutation distribution.
what_exists: lineage genomes = rows of interaction matrix A_i,:
mechanisms.what_changes: at reproduction, offspring edge weights = parent weights + noise whose variance/mean bias scales with (e*-e_i(t)).
mechanisms.what_persists: the baseline resource 'menu' (topology of accessible edges) across generations; only weights and active-edge selection mutate.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: downstream fitness selects surviving lineages, but this mechanism concerns variation generation prior to selection.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: species reproduce with deficit-gated mutation at biomass-threshold reproduction events.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: population-level exploration of edge-weight space is biased toward resolving energetic deficits — a directed-variation analog of learning.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the gating rule should accelerate deficit resolution across any resource-menu topology, testable in multiple network configurations.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: per-lineage deficit magnitude should correlate with per-lineage mutation step size under gating, unlike state-blind mutation with matched aggregate variance.
mechanisms.minimal_world: 5-species community with an 8-edge resource menu per species; intervention implements deficit-gated mutation, tracking e_i(t) and edge-weight change events. Null twin: same aggregate mutation-rate statistics (matched total variance) but mutation direction/magnitude drawn independent of e_i(t); no deficit-magnitude/mutation-size correlation should appear in the null.

mechanisms.statement: Effective per-capita interaction strength is a function of current standing energy flux through the shared edge and ambient system-wide throughput, so the community Jacobian is a nonlinear function of full state and flux history; identical instantaneous states reached via different flux histories yield different local stability, which fixed-coefficient models cannot reproduce.
mechanisms.what_changes: a_ij(t+1)=a_ij(t)+eta*(target_phi - phi_ij(t)), coupling coefficient drift to flux-homeostatic targets.
mechanisms.what_persists: the functional form of the adaptation rule persists as fixed structure even as coefficient values drift.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none; this is a law, not a selection process.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: standard population growth continues at the x_i level.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: coupling coefficients adapt toward flux-homeostatic targets within a lifetime, distinct from cross-generational mutation.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the hysteresis signature in a_ij vs. history should reappear in the same motif embedded in different larger networks.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the community Jacobian's dominant eigenvalue at a fixed state x* should differ depending on the flux-history path taken to reach x*, unlike fixed-coefficient models which predict identical Jacobian at identical x.
mechanisms.minimal_world: 2-species predator-prey motif with adaptive a_ij(t), driven along two different trajectories converging on the same x* with different flux histories; intervention measures Jacobian eigenvalues at x* on both paths. Null twin: fixed-coefficient model parameterized at the time-averaged a_ij value across both trajectories; the null predicts identical Jacobian at x* regardless of path.

mechanisms.statement: A community cannot occupy any attractor whose aggregate metabolic demand exceeds currently sustainable energy input plus storage; this carves the attractor landscape into reachable and energetically forbidden regions independent of local Lyapunov stability, so a locally stable attractor can be globally inaccessible.
mechanisms.what_changes: if total demand Dtot(t)=sum m_i x_i(t) exceeds I(t)+S(t), a forced proportional die-off reduces x_i until feasible; S(t+1)=S(t)+I(t)-Dtot(t).
mechanisms.what_persists: the mathematical identity of {A_k} as fixed points of the unconstrained vector field persists even as reachability changes.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none directly; this constraint defines the feasible set within which selection (mechanism 4) operates.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: species reproduce subject to starvation correction.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: none; pure constraint.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the forbidden/reachable partition should be identical across different initial conditions sharing the same metabolic-demand vector and I(t) schedule.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the system should show a recurrent sawtooth-like deflection pattern around a high-demand attractor A* rather than exponential divergence, distinguishing constrained infeasibility from ordinary Jacobian instability.
mechanisms.minimal_world: 3-species community with a genuinely locally-stable A* requiring high aggregate biomass; intervention sets I(t) below A*'s demand and observes trajectory shape. Null twin: same dynamics but A* engineered as a genuinely unstable fixed point (positive Jacobian eigenvalue) with I(t) unconstrained, tuned so divergence rate matches the sawtooth amplitude/frequency — trajectory shape (sawtooth vs. exponential divergence) distinguishes the two.

mechanisms.statement: A strongly connected keystone node projects high-dimensional community dynamics onto a low-dimensional attractor manifold, whose effective dimension (participation ratio of Jacobian eigenvalues) is set by the keystone's coupling strength; this compressed representation is causally load-bearing, collapsing when the keystone is removed rather than being a mere statistical artifact.
what_exists: interaction matrix A with a designated keystone node
mechanisms.what_changes: standard dynamics x_{t+1}=x_t+x_t*(r-Ax_t); d_eff(t)=(sum lambda_i)^2/sum(lambda_i^2) is tracked continuously from J(x(t)).
mechanisms.what_persists: the low-rank structure of effective community dynamics persists while keystone edges remain intact.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none; this is a representation, not a selection process.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: standard population reproduction.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: an external predictor can reconstruct the trajectory from d_eff-many coordinates while the keystone is present but requires many more after removal.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a predictor trained on pre-removal low-dimensional trajectory should fail to generalize post-removal without retraining/expanding dimensionality.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: rank-r reconstruction error at fixed r should sharply increase upon keystone removal but not upon removal of a high-biomass, dynamically peripheral decoy node.
mechanisms.minimal_world: 8-species community with one strongly-coupled keystone and one high-biomass but weakly-coupled decoy; intervention removes each separately, recomputing d_eff and reconstruction error. Null twin: removal of the biomass-decoy node (matched in biomass/abundance-variance to the keystone) — negligible d_eff change should occur in this null.

mechanisms.statement: Synaptic (or parameter) updates are gated by the magnitude of a local prediction error rather than applied at a fixed rate, so learning accelerates when the world becomes unpredictable and freezes when predictions are accurate. This produces automatic reallocation of plasticity toward currently informative statistics without any global schedule.
mechanisms.what_changes: W <- W + eta * g(|e_t|) * e_t * s_{t-1}^T, where g is an increasing gating function of error magnitude (three-factor rule)
mechanisms.what_persists: accumulated weight structure encoding stable statistical regularities once error is small
mechanisms.what_is_selected: connections whose updates repeatedly reduce error are reinforced; connections that don't are left unchanged
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable; single learner, no reproduction
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a predictive mapping from past to future states of the environment
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: weights trained under one regime transfer to a new but statistically related regime, enabling faster re-convergence than starting from scratch
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: after an abrupt change in environmental statistics, error-gated learning shows a transient spike in effective learning rate and faster re-convergence than a fixed-rate Hebbian rule matched for total cumulative weight change
mechanisms.minimal_world: A symbolic sequence world with a fixed transition matrix; agent predicts next symbol and updates W using the error-gated rule. Intervention: switch the transition matrix at t=500. Null twin: identical architecture and total weight-change budget but with constant learning rate (ungated), tuned so average |ΔW| over the whole run matches the gated model; compare re-adaptation speed after the switch.

mechanisms.statement: A stochastic encoder maps inputs into a low-dimensional latent code trained to minimize its mutual information with the raw input while maximizing mutual information with a downstream target, via a rate-distortion tradeoff (I(Z;X) - beta*I(Z;Y)). This forces the system to discover the minimal sufficient statistic of the input for the task, discarding task-irrelevant variation.
mechanisms.what_changes: encoder/decoder parameters updated by gradient descent on the variational bottleneck objective; beta controls compression pressure
mechanisms.what_persists: the subset of latent dimensions carrying Y-relevant information persists across training; irrelevant dimensions collapse toward the prior
mechanisms.what_is_selected: latent dimensions/features with high I(Z;Y) per unit I(Z;X) are selected; nuisance-correlated dimensions are suppressed
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable to a single system; the encoder architecture can be copied wholesale as a unit
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a minimal sufficient representation for predicting Y from X
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the compressed code transfers to new inputs where nuisance variation differs but the Y-relevant structure is preserved
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: an I(Z;X) vs I(Z;Y) tradeoff curve showing a sharp compression phase transition as beta increases, and superior generalization under nuisance-distribution shift, compared to a plain autoencoder of equal latent dimensionality with no beta term
mechanisms.minimal_world: Synthetic vectors X = concat(relevant_bits, nuisance_bits) + noise, with Y = f(relevant_bits). Intervention: at test time increase nuisance dimensionality/variance beyond training range. Null twin: an autoencoder with identical latent size trained only to reconstruct X (beta effectively 0), matched capacity and training loss on Y-prediction via a separate readout, but retaining nuisance info — expected to generalize worse under the nuisance shift.

mechanisms.statement: Internal belief states evolve continuously via gradient descent on a variational free energy functional that combines precision-weighted sensory prediction error with a complexity cost on deviation from prior beliefs. This creates attractor dynamics in belief space that infer hidden causes rather than merely reacting to instantaneous error.
what_exists: generative mapping g(mu) predicting sensory signal
mechanisms.what_changes: mu_dot = -dF/dmu where F = pi*(s - g(mu))^2 + complexity(mu, prior)
mechanisms.what_persists: attractor structure/fixed points of the belief dynamics and the generative model g across trials
mechanisms.what_is_selected: belief trajectories that reduce free energy persist; higher-F trajectories are damped out by the gradient flow
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable
mechanisms.what_can_learn: slow adaptation of g's parameters to reduce long-run average free energy (learning the generative model)
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: learned prior/generative structure transfers to new environments sharing the same hidden-cause statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: under ambiguous or bistable stimuli, the gradient-flow model shows hysteresis (percept depends on recent history) and characteristic relaxation time scaling with precision, unlike a reactive controller
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 1D hidden oscillatory phase generates noisy sensory readings; the model infers phase via gradient descent on F. Intervention: introduce an ambiguous/bistable stimulus segment and a sudden phase jump. Null twin: a PID-like controller that minimizes instantaneous error only (no inferred hidden state, no complexity term), matched steady-state error — predicted to lack hysteresis and the characteristic gradual relaxation curve.

mechanisms.statement: A population of coding units competes via lateral inhibition so that only a sparse subset is active for any input, and only active units update their receptive fields toward the current input (winner-take-most Hebbian learning). This yields an overcomplete but sparse dictionary of reusable features rather than a fully distributed code.

mechanisms.what_persists: receptive fields tuned to frequently recurring input features persist and refine over time
mechanisms.what_is_selected: units whose current weights best match frequent input patterns win the competition repeatedly and get sharpened; rarely-winning units remain unspecialized or get reset
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: optionally, an overused/high-variance unit can be duplicated/split into two specialized units
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a sparse dictionary of basis features spanning the input distribution
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the learned sparse code transfers to compress and reconstruct novel inputs sharing the same underlying feature statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: reconstruction accuracy and code sparsity (kurtosis) under novel combinations of familiar features, compared to a fully distributed dense code of equal total weight norm and unit count without inhibition
mechanisms.minimal_world: A world of small bar/patch stimuli combined additively; network learns a sparse code via lateral inhibition. Intervention: present novel overlapping combinations at test time. Null twin: identical unit count and weight-update rule but without lateral inhibition, so all units update on every input (dense distributed code), matched total activation energy — measure interference/catastrophic overlap versus the sparse model.

mechanisms.statement: A population undergoes a Moran-like process: at each step one individual is replaced by a copy of another individual chosen with probability proportional to measured task fitness, with mutation applied to the copy. mechanisms.what_is_selected: genotypes yielding higher task fitness are selected for increased reproduction

mechanisms.what_can_transfer: successful genotype motifs transfer to descendants via reproduction across generations

mechanisms.statement: The mutation operator can duplicate an existing genomic module (a self-contained functional subunit) and apply elevated mutation rate to the copy while leaving the original intact, occasionally also deleting redundant modules. mechanisms.what_persists: essential modules whose deletion is lethal are retained through selective filtering
mechanisms.what_is_selected: duplicated modules that acquire a beneficial new subfunction are retained; non-beneficial duplicates are pruned by selection or drift
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: modules replicate within the genome; whole organisms reproduce carrying the genome to offspring
mechanisms.what_can_learn: not direct learning but evolvability: increased capacity to acquire new subfunctions across generations
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a module's subfunction transfers to new contexts within the genome (reuse across tasks) once duplicated and repurposed
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: rate of acquisition of new functional capability and degree of modular reuse (measured as functional independence/shared-module usage across tasks) compared to a null twin restricted to point mutations only, at matched total mutation rate
mechanisms.minimal_world: Agents with modular genomes solving several related subtasks (e.g., composed motor primitives) over generations. Null twin: mutation operator limited to point mutations at matched overall mutation-rate budget — measure time-to-innovation and module-reuse rate difference on the new subtask.

mechanisms.statement: Beliefs are nodes in a signed weighted graph of justificatory support/conflict edges; a newly proposed hypothesis is inserted as a node and its credence is determined by iterative relaxation (constraint satisfaction) toward a network-wide fixed point, not by an isolated score. mechanisms.statement: A system continuously updates its internal parameters to reduce the mismatch between predicted and actual sensory input, with the update direction set by the local gradient of squared prediction error. Over time this produces internal models that anticipate regularities in the input stream. No external label is required; the error signal itself is the only teacher.
mechanisms.what_changes: w is updated each step by w <- w - lr * d(e_t^2)/dw; p_t changes as w changes.
mechanisms.what_persists: weight configurations that have driven error down persist and accumulate across steps.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: parameter directions that reduce cumulative squared error are reinforced; directions that increase it are damped.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: None; this is a single-system adaptive law, not a population process.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the temporal/statistical structure of the sensory generator, enabling multi-step-ahead prediction.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the learned predictive weights transfer to new sequences drawn from the same generative process (new phase, new instance, same statistics).
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: weight-update vectors correlate with the *sign* of the local error gradient, producing monotonically decreasing error autocorrelation over training, unlike an error-triggered random-walk-with-acceptance rule that can match the same average error trajectory but shows no gradient-sign correlation.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 1D periodic signal generator (sine plus small noise) feeds a scalar predictor with a few weights. Intervention: shift the generator's phase mid-run and measure re-adaptation speed. Null twin: same predictor, same average error-reduction schedule, but weights are updated via random perturbation accepted only if error decreases (an accept/reject search) tuned to match the mean error curve exactly, removing gradient-direction information while preserving nuisance statistics.

mechanisms.statement: The environment provides two resource types whose spatial abundance is anti-correlated, and intake follows diminishing returns for any single trait allocation. This rule alone, without any social interaction, creates selective pressure for organisms to specialize their intake-trait allocation to local resource ratios rather than remaining generalists.

agent traits (e1,e2) with e1+e2 fixed budget
mechanisms.what_changes: energy(t+1) = energy(t) + sqrt(e1*R1(x,y)) + sqrt(e2*R2(x,y)); agents move toward higher local energy gradient; traits mutate slightly at reproduction.
mechanisms.what_persists: the anti-correlated spatial resource structure across generations.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: trait pairs (e1,e2) whose match to local resource ratio maximizes intake are favored in reproduction.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: agents reproduce proportional to accumulated energy, offspring inherit (e1,e2) with mutation.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: individuals can additionally learn a movement policy that follows the local resource gradient within a lifetime.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: specialization pattern (bimodal trait distribution) transfers to novel landscapes sharing the same anti-correlation structure, even with different absolute abundances.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: the population trait distribution becomes bimodal (specialists) under spatial segregation of resources but stays unimodal (generalist) when the identical total resources are mixed uniformly at every location — same total resource budget, different spatial layout.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A grid where two resources are placed either in separated patches (test) or uniformly interleaved at every cell (null twin), with total resource mass held equal between conditions. Agents with mutable (e1,e2) forage, gain energy via diminishing-returns intake, and reproduce. Measure trait-distribution modality after many generations in both layouts.

mechanisms.statement: A mutation inserts (or removes) a single rank-1 component in a CP-decomposed natural-parameter tensor (or a TT bond-dimension increment), after which the MaxEnt dual multipliers are re-solved to restore constraint satisfaction under the new capacity, isolating the discrete 'entropy cost of one unit of capacity.'
mechanisms.what_exists: A CP/TT decomposed natural-parameter tensor of rank R; a newly inserted candidate component; a dual-ascent re-optimizer restoring constraint matching after each mutation.
mechanisms.what_changes: Rank changes by ±1 per mutation; all factors and dual multipliers are re-optimized to reconvergence under the fixed constraint set.
mechanisms.what_persists: The constraint set persists across mutations; pre-existing components are perturbed by re-optimization rather than discarded (unless targeted for removal).
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Mutations yielding the largest entropy gain (insertion) or smallest loss (removal) per unit rank change are preferred in a hill-climbing search.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: A successful inserted component becomes a stable parent that can be duplicated-and-perturbed to generate the next candidate mutation.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The accepted-mutation sequence learns an efficient low-to-high-rank curriculum toward the full-rank MaxEnt solution.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: The discovered ordered component sequence can initialize a related but non-identical constraint set.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Entropy gained per mutation as a function of rank shows discontinuous 'cliffs' at algebraic identifiability (Kruskal-rank) thresholds, absent in a naive least-squares rank-increment (no entropy dual) whose error-reduction curve is smooth and monotone.
mechanisms.minimal_world: Four ternary variables with target third-order marginals requiring true CP rank 4. Intervention: insert-then-reoptimize from rank 1 to 8 and remove-then-reoptimize from 8 to 1, recording entropy gain/loss to detect a cliff near rank 4. Null twin: identical rank-increment procedure but with Frobenius-norm least-squares refit instead of entropy re-optimization; its curve should lack the cliff.

mechanisms.statement: Starting from rank 1, a system repeatedly proposes candidate rank-1 additions but accepts an addition only if the resulting entropy gain per added parameter exceeds a fixed threshold τ; growth autonomously halts once no candidate clears τ, yielding an emergent 'critical rank' matching the true generative complexity.
mechanisms.what_exists: A growing CP/TT decomposition, a running parameter tally, a fixed target constraint set, and a threshold τ.
mechanisms.what_changes: At each step, several candidate additions are proposed, dual-optimized, and the best entropy-gain-per-parameter is compared to τ; if above, rank increments, else development halts.
mechanisms.what_persists: τ persists as the sole external control on final complexity; accepted components persist and may be fine-tuned.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Among proposed candidates at a step, the one with greatest entropy-gain-per-parameter is permanently incorporated.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: The current model's accepted-component sequence can be inherited wholesale by an offspring run with a different τ, stopping earlier or later along the same lineage.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The system learns its own required representational complexity purely from the entropy-gain signal.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: The final halted rank can be transferred as a size hyperparameter suggestion for a related constraint set.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Final halted rank vs. τ shows a plateau anchored at the true generative rank R*, reflecting the entropy-gain cliff of the mutation mechanism; a validation-error-plateau stopping rule using raw reconstruction error instead shows a smoothly drifting relationship with no such anchored plateau.
mechanisms.minimal_world: Same four-ternary-variable, true-rank-4 world as the mutation mechanism. Intervention: run entropy-gain-gated growth across many seeds and a τ sweep, recording final rank. Null twin: identical growth gated on Frobenius reconstruction-error improvement per parameter instead of entropy; its final-rank-vs-threshold curve should lack the rank-4 plateau.

mechanisms.statement: In a TT-format MaxEnt model, contracting the chain left-to-right versus right-to-left should yield identical marginals/partition function at a true fixed point; when bond duals are only locally optimized, the two directions disagree, and this disagreement can drive a self-correction of bond factors without access to the true target distribution.
mechanisms.what_exists: A TT chain of cores with per-bond dual variables; forward and backward contraction procedures; a discrepancy signal defined as their difference.
mechanisms.what_changes: Bond factors are updated proportionally to the local forward-backward discrepancy, iterated until discrepancy vanishes along the chain.
mechanisms.what_persists: The chain topology persists; only core values and discrepancy magnitude change over correction iterations.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: Bonds with the largest discrepancy are prioritized for correction first.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: A converged, discrepancy-free bond structure can serve as a validated template copied into a new chain of the same length.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The system learns to detect and repair its own local inconsistency from a purely internally generated signal.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: The discrepancy-correction procedure transfers unchanged to TT chains of any length or alphabet size, depending only on topology.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Total forward-backward discrepancy decays monotonically to near zero, with final entropy matching a fully globally-solved MaxEnt dual on the same TT family; correcting bonds in a random direction of matched step size fails to converge discrepancy or recover matched entropy.
mechanisms.minimal_world: A chain of five binary variables with known TT bond-dimension-2 structure. Intervention: initialize with under-converged block-updated duals, then apply discrepancy correction, tracking discrepancy and entropy. Null twin: identical step-size schedule but random-direction corrections of matched norm; discrepancy should not systematically decay.

mechanisms.statement: Forcing a maximum-entropy solution into TT format with a fixed variable ordering imposes a Markov-chain conditional independence structure consistent with that order; scanning orderings and recording achievable entropy at fixed bond dimension reveals which ordering aligns with the true generative causal chain, since the true order requires the least bond capacity.
mechanisms.what_exists: k discrete variables; a permutation defining TT mode order; a TT-MaxEnt model under that ordering at fixed bond dimension; a shared, ordering-independent target constraint set.
mechanisms.what_changes: For each candidate permutation, the TT-format dual-ascent solver is run to convergence, producing an entropy/violation pair.
mechanisms.what_persists: The constraint set and bond dimension budget persist identically across all tested permutations.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: The permutation achieving lowest violation/highest entropy at fixed bond dimension is selected as the inferred causal order.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: The winning ordering seeds a local-search round of neighboring permutation swaps.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: The procedure learns an ordering hypothesis purely from the entropy-compressibility interaction, with no explicit temporal labels.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: An inferred good ordering can be tested as a prior ordering when new variables are inserted into an extended chain.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: Achieved entropy at fixed bond dimension peaks at (or near) the true generative order with a measurable gap to other orderings; a purely correlational criterion (total matched pairwise mutual information) fails to single out the true order distinctly, since many permutations can match the same pairwise correlations without matching chain compressibility.
mechanisms.minimal_world: Six binary variables generated by a true Markov chain X1→...→X6. Intervention: for many/all permutations, fit TT-MaxEnt at fixed bond dimension 2 to shared marginal constraints, recording entropy per permutation and checking whether the true order is the maximizer. Null twin: matched-marginal data drawn from a fully symmetric, order-invariant interaction structure; the identical permutation scan should show a flat entropy landscape with no distinguished maximizer.
