mechanisms.statement: A sparse-coding Kalman filter is trained with a joint loss that adds metamorphic-relation violation (e.g., scaling the input should scale the sparse code's active coefficients by the same factor, without changing its support) to the standard reconstruction/prediction error. This creates a training signal that exists only because a transform algebra is imposed on top of sparse coding and filtering; neither component alone produces it.
mechanisms.what_exists: latent state x_t, sparse code a_t with dictionary Phi, observation y_t=Phi a_t+noise, Kalman matrices (A,Q,C,R), a fixed set of transforms T={scale_c, shift_s, reverse, permute} with declared expected effects T' on a_t.
mechanisms.what_changes: Phi and the Kalman gain K are updated each step by gradient descent on L = ||y-Phi a||^2 + lambda*sum_T ||encode(T(y)) - T'(encode(y))||^2.
mechanisms.what_persists: the transform set T and its declared expected mappings T' (the algebra is fixed across training).
mechanisms.what_is_selected: dictionary atoms and gain entries that jointly minimize reconstruction and relation-violation loss are retained with larger weight; others shrink toward zero.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: none directly; coefficients are reweighted, not replicated.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the dictionary Phi, the Kalman gain schedule, and the relative weight lambda between reconstruction and relation terms.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a Phi trained under relation loss should generalize to unseen scale/shift ranges without retraining, since atoms were shaped to satisfy T' rather than only fit training-range statistics.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: measure reconstruction error growth when test inputs are scaled beyond the training range; a system trained with lambda>0 should show markedly slower error growth than an identical system with lambda=0, despite equal in-distribution loss.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: 1-D latent Gaussian random walk generating sparse overcomplete observations of length 20. Intervention: train two identical filters, one with lambda>0 (relation loss active), one with lambda=0, on the same trajectories; then test both on trajectories scaled by factors outside the training range. Null twin: a system trained with lambda=0 but given extra reconstruction-only training epochs equal in compute to the relation-loss runs, so total gradient steps and data exposure match but no transform algebra is ever invoked.

mechanisms.statement: Each dictionary atom accumulates a survival score equal to the number of metamorphic relations it satisfies when its associated code coefficient is transformed and re-encoded. Atoms whose survival score falls below a threshold across a sliding window are replaced by resampled atoms; this is a Darwinian filter on dictionary composition driven purely by relation-passing, not by reconstruction fitness.
mechanisms.what_exists: dictionary atoms phi_i, per-atom survival counters, code coefficients a_i,t, transform set T, a replacement pool of candidate random atoms.
mechanisms.what_changes: at each evaluation epoch, survival counters increment/decrement per relation pass/fail; atoms below threshold are deleted and replaced by mutated copies of high-scoring survivors.
mechanisms.what_persists: the identity and survival history of atoms that keep passing relations across epochs.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: atoms with high relation-pass counts, independent of their contribution to reconstruction error magnitude.
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: high-scoring atoms reproduce (with small perturbation) to refill slots vacated by low-scoring atoms.
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the dictionary composition evolves toward a subset of atoms that are jointly equivariant under T.
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a dictionary selected this way should port to a new but structurally related transform group (e.g., new scale range) better than one selected purely by reconstruction error.
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: compare the fraction of atoms retained after transfer to a shifted transform group between relation-selected and reconstruction-selected dictionaries; relation-selection predicts higher retained/reused fraction.
mechanisms.minimal_world: World: a 30-atom overcomplete dictionary over 10-D sparse codes generating 2-D observations. Intervention: run relation-based culling (replace bottom 20% by survival score every N steps) versus reconstruction-error-based culling (replace atoms with highest average reconstruction residual). Null twin: reconstruction-error-culled dictionary trained on identical data schedule and identical total number of atom replacements, so churn rate and data exposure match but the culling criterion never references any transform.

mechanisms.what_persists: the minimum k found to be 'relation-sufficient' persists as the operating capacity across subsequent episodes with similar transform demands.
mechanisms.what_is_selected: unit-additions that buy relation-consistency per unit of added capacity are kept; additions that only buy reconstruction accuracy are rejected.

mechanisms.statement: Local morphogen concentration continuously sets the sliding modification threshold of a BCM-style Hebbian rule, so identical coincident activity produces potentiation in high-morphogen regions and depression in low-morphogen regions. mechanisms.statement: Repeated correlated activity locally up-regulates a slow-decaying morphogen trace, distinct from the fast synaptic weights, so the trace's spatial profile becomes a durable record of past correlated-activity sites. If weights are subsequently erased (lesion, reset), new Hebbian synapse growth is biased toward high-trace locations, regenerating the original connectivity pattern from the trace alone.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: high-T locations are favored during regrowth (soft selection on new synapse placement)
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the original weight pattern can be regenerated from T after a wipe, i.e., the pattern reproduces itself via the trace
mechanisms.what_can_learn: T is continuously learned from ongoing correlated activity, serving as implicit long-term memory beneath w

Measure correlation between pre-lesion and post-regrowth weight maps. Null twin: identical reset and identical regrowth input, but T is held at zero / uniform (no accumulated trace, matched total morphogen budget spent instead as a flat non-informative field) — post-regrowth map should then correlate only with the new input, not the original.

mechanisms.statement: Growth cones follow a morphogen gradient to a coarse target zone (chemoaffinity) before any activity-dependent refinement occurs; only within that zone does Hebbian competition refine fine connectivity. The gradient thus causally restricts the set of eligible partners available to Hebbian competition, independent of what activity statistics later occur.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: within S, subsets of synapses win or lose via correlation-based competition (e.g., winner-take-all normalization)
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the coarse map is deterministically reproducible from the gradient alone across different activity-seed runs
mechanisms.what_can_learn: fine receptive-field structure within each topographic zone is learned from activity
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the coarse map transfers across any activity statistics (invariant); fine structure is activity-specific and does not transfer
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: shuffling activity correlation structure while holding the gradient fixed changes only within-zone fine structure and leaves the coarse map intact; a pure-Hebbian null model without a guidance gradient would show the coarse map itself reorganizing when activity statistics are shuffled
mechanisms.minimal_world: A layer of source neurons projects growth cones toward a target sheet under a fixed guidance gradient, forming candidate zone-restricted synapse sets; Hebbian competition then refines weights within each zone under one of several different activity-correlation regimes. Intervention: gradient present, guiding zone assignment. Measure zone assignment stability and within-zone fine structure across activity regimes. Null twin: same target sheet, same number of candidate synapses and same activity regimes, but zone assignment is instead randomized independent of any gradient (matched statistics of connections per zone) — coarse map should then vary across activity regimes since nothing anchors it.

mechanisms.statement: Each neuron acquires a scalar identity equal to its local morphogen concentration read out at a fixed developmental time; because spontaneous activity correlation is stronger between neurons of similar identity (e.g., via propagating waves), Hebbian plasticity preferentially strengthens same-identity connections. The result is a representation in which continuous positional identity is encoded entirely in synaptic community/graph structure, with no explicit coordinate ever stored.

activity correlation as a decreasing function of |m_i - m_j|
mechanisms.what_changes: dw_ij/dt = eta*corr(i,j)*Hebb_term, where corr(i,j) depends on |m_i - m_j|
mechanisms.what_persists: community structure of the weight graph continues to encode the rank/metric order of m_i even after m is no longer read anywhere
mechanisms.what_is_selected: edges between similar-identity neurons are retained; dissimilar-identity edges are pruned toward zero
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the assortative wiring scheme can be reapplied to impose the same encoding on a naive network given only the activity-correlation rule
mechanisms.what_can_learn: fine edge weights are learned from specific activity draws; the encoding scheme itself is the transferable, learned regularity
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a decoder trained only on graph structure (no access to m_i) generalizes to reconstruct positional order in novel identity distributions
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: decodability of original positional order from connectivity graph alone (e.g., spectral embedding correlating with m_i), versus a null model where wiring depends on activity unrelated to m_i, giving chance-level decodability
mechanisms.minimal_world: N neurons are assigned identity values m_i drawn from a fixed distribution; spontaneous activity correlation between i,j is generated as a Gaussian function of |m_i-m_j| with fixed total correlation budget. Hebbian learning wires the network. Intervention: correlation depends on m_i. Measure decoding accuracy of m_i order from final graph spectral embedding. Null twin: same total correlation statistics (same marginal correlation distribution across all pairs) but correlations randomly permuted across pairs, decoupled from m_i — decoding accuracy should drop to chance.

mechanisms.statement: A diffusible trophic resource is produced at a constant background rate and consumed by synapses in proportion to their activity-driven uptake; a synapse can only grow in weight if local resource exceeds a threshold. Because active synapses locally deplete the resource, this produces long-range effective inhibition through diffusion-limited competition alone, without any dedicated inhibitory molecule, and predicts a minimum spacing between surviving strong synapses.
mechanisms.what_changes: dR/dt = sigma - kappa*u*R + D*Laplacian(R) ; dw/dt = eta*c*R*(1-w) - decay
mechanisms.what_persists: a minimal exclusion distance between mature high-weight synapses, set by D/kappa, robust to changes in correlation magnitude
mechanisms.what_is_selected: synapses that first draw down local resource suppress nearby competitors from crossing the growth threshold — a first-past-the-post selection among near-equal initial competitors
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the exclusion-zone spacing tiles identically if the tissue area is expanded
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the system organizes spatial winner placement from initial correlation noise, not stimulus content per se
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the minimum-spacing statistic transfers across different absolute correlation magnitudes, depending only on D/kappa
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: pairwise distance distribution of surviving strong synapses shows a hard minimum-distance exclusion zone, versus a null model with resource-independent competitive normalization (e.g., plain Oja's rule) where spacing instead scales with correlation/noise magnitude rather than a fixed diffusion-set minimum
mechanisms.minimal_world: A line of candidate synapses with near-identical initial weights and matched independent activity-correlation noise competes for a shared diffusing resource. Intervention: resource field as above. Measure nearest-neighbor spacing distribution of final strong synapses across many noise seeds and varying correlation magnitude. Null twin: same activity/noise statistics and same mean total 'inhibitory budget', but competition implemented as instantaneous non-diffusing normalization (weights renormalized to fixed sum at each step, no spatial R field) — spacing should then depend on noise magnitude rather than being pinned to a fixed diffusion-length minimum.

mechanisms.statement: Neurons release a diffusible corrective signal proportional to the deviation of their firing rate from a target set-point; this signal diffuses locally and multiplicatively rescales the Hebbian learning rate, down where local activity is too high and up where too low. This produces spatially patterned homeostatic domains whose size is set by the corrector's diffusion length rather than by any single-neuron rule.
mechanisms.what_changes: dC/dt = kappa*e - beta*C + D*Laplacian(C) ; dw/dt = eta*(1 - gamma*C)*Hebb_term
mechanisms.what_persists: the characteristic homeostatic domain size sqrt(D/beta), stable across different Hebbian learning rates
mechanisms.what_is_selected: none — continuous negative feedback, not discrete selection
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the domain-size statistic re-forms identically under resampled activity with the same underlying statistics
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the network keeps firing-rate deviation bounded while still permitting local Hebbian differentiation within each domain
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the diffusion-length-set domain scale transfers across different target activity levels or input statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: spatial autocorrelation of firing-rate deviation shows a characteristic correlation length matching sqrt(D/beta) independent of input strength, versus a null model using purely local (non-diffusive) synaptic scaling, which shows no spatial correlation structure in deviations beyond single-neuron scale
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 2D sheet of neurons receives spatially patchy input drive of varying strength; Hebbian learning runs alongside the corrective field. Intervention: C diffuses per the PDE above. Measure spatial autocorrelation length of firing-rate deviation at steady state across different D values. Null twin: same total corrective 'budget' per neuron and same target rate, but corrective scaling computed purely locally per-neuron (synaptic scaling with no diffusion term, D=0) with matched mean correction magnitude — spatial autocorrelation of deviations should collapse to near-zero beyond one neuron's width.

mechanisms.statement: A synapse's Hebbian weight change only consolidates into a long-term stable value if correlated activity co-occurs with local morphogen concentration inside a narrow permissive band; outside that band, weight changes are transient and decay back to baseline. This creates a bottleneck in which only activity patterns temporally aligned with the correct positional/developmental-stage signal can become permanent memory.
what_exists: gate indicator b(x,t) = 1 if M(x,t) in [theta1,theta2]
mechanisms.what_changes: dw_t/dt = eta*Hebb - w_t/tau_fast ; dw_c/dt = b(x,t)*kappa*w_t - w_c/tau_slow
mechanisms.what_persists: only w_c values reinforced during b=1 windows survive long-term; everything else reverts to baseline
mechanisms.what_is_selected: activity patterns temporally aligned with the correct positional gate are selected for permanence; misaligned patterns are filtered out
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: consolidated structure can in principle be 'replayed' into another gated region to reproduce an equivalent stable pattern if gate timing matches
mechanisms.what_can_learn: which specific correlated inputs get permanently encoded is learned, but capacity is bottlenecked by gate width/duration
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the bottleneck constraint (what qualifies as consolidatable) transfers across different specific input contents, since it depends only on gate timing
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: narrowing the morphogen permissive band reduces the number of distinct consolidated patterns retained even when total training time/activity is held constant; a null model with content-independent, always-on consolidation (band spans all M) shows retention scaling only with training time, not with gate width
mechanisms.minimal_world: A set of independent synapse channels each receive their own transient correlated-activity episodes over a fixed training duration, with M(x,t) varying across channels so each has a different fraction of time inside [theta1,theta2]. Intervention: consolidation gated by b(x,t). Measure number of channels with non-baseline w_c at the end, as a function of gate width. Null twin: identical training episodes and total duration, but consolidation always enabled (b=1 always, matched average kappa*duration to equal total consolidation 'dose') — retained-pattern count should then depend only on training time, not on any band width parameter.

mechanisms.statement: Each synapse is assigned a fitness score equal to the product of its Hebbian correlation strength and a positional-compatibility term derived from the difference between pre- and postsynaptic morphogen identities; synapses below a joint fitness threshold are pruned each round while survivors proliferate nearby branches. This produces an ocular-dominance-like segregated map that requires both factors together and cannot arise from either alone.
what_exists: synapse population with correlation score c_ij
mechanisms.what_changes: each round, synapses with F_ij < theta_p are removed; survivors sprout additional nearby synapses sharing the same identity-pairing bias
mechanisms.what_persists: the final segregated domain topology (stripe/patch width and identity registration) persists after pruning ends and activity ceases
mechanisms.what_is_selected: individual synapses are selected for survival/proliferation based on the joint score F_ij each round
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: surviving synapses sprout further synapses carrying the same identity-pairing bias, propagating the segregated pattern spatially
mechanisms.what_can_learn: exact stripe/domain boundary locations are a contingent joint outcome of initial correlation noise and gradient calibration
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the qualitative requirement that segregation needs both factors together is a transferable prediction across different gradient shapes and activity statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: knocking out either factor alone (flattening the gradient so p_ij=1 for all pairs, or decorrelating activity so c_ij=const) abolishes registered segregation in this model; a correlation-only classic ocular-dominance-style null model (no positional term) still produces stripe-like segregation from correlation alone, but boundary locations are uncorrelated with any underlying gradient coordinate across repeated runs, whereas the joint mechanism reliably registers boundaries to the gradient coordinate
mechanisms.minimal_world: A population of afferent synapses from two input sources connects to a target sheet carrying a fixed morphogen identity gradient; input-source-correlated activity and identity difference jointly determine F_ij each pruning round across many independent runs. Intervention: full joint model as above. Measure across-run consistency of stripe boundary position relative to the gradient coordinate. Null twin: same afferents, same activity-correlation statistics, same total number of pruning rounds and pruning rate, but p_ij fixed at a constant matching its mean value (identity/gradient term removed, only c_ij drives pruning) — segregated stripes may still appear from correlation alone, but their boundary position relative to the (now causally inert) gradient coordinate should be uncorrelated across runs.

mechanisms.statement: System state updates along a step scaled by the locally estimated input-output Jacobian norm rather than a fixed learning rate: regions of high sensitivity get smaller, more cautious updates and regions of low sensitivity get larger updates. This produces adaptive step-size dynamics that automatically slow exploration where small input changes cause large output swings.
mechanisms.what_changes: x_{t+1} = x_t - eta_t * grad, where eta_t = eta0 / (1+||J(x_t)||); J is re-estimated each step via finite differences on a small perturbation batch
mechanisms.what_persists: the running estimate of J across nearby states (smoothed via exponential average)
mechanisms.what_is_selected: trajectories that reach low-loss regions without oscillation are retained in a policy comparison
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the step-size adaptation rule itself can be copied to new state dimensions added later
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the mapping from local curvature/sensitivity to step size, tuned across many trajectories
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the learned eta(x)-vs-J(x) relationship transfers to new loss landscapes with similar local geometry
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: compare convergence path curvature and update variance against fixed-step gradient descent on the same landscape; sensitivity-scaled version should show reduced update-to-update variance in high-curvature regions without loss of overall convergence speed
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 2D quadratic-plus-ridge loss surface with one steep direction and one shallow direction; the intervention perturbs the steepness of the ridge mid-run. The mechanism world re-estimates J and adapts eta; the null twin uses a fixed learning rate matched to have the same average step size over the whole run, so total path length statistics match but per-region adaptivity is absent.

mechanisms.statement: The world is a fixed causal graph of nodes with weighted edges; a perturbation injected at any node propagates through edges with signal decaying by an edge-specific attenuation factor. The resulting downstream variance profile across nodes, given many random perturbations, defines an intrinsic 'sensitivity field' over the graph.
what_exists: directed weighted edges with attenuation factors
mechanisms.what_changes: on each propagation step, node value updates as weighted sum of parent perturbations times edge attenuation, iterated until decay below threshold
mechanisms.what_persists: the graph topology and edge weights across perturbation trials
mechanisms.what_is_selected: graphs whose sensitivity field concentrates variance on a small predictable subset of nodes are retained in a comparison across many random graphs
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: subgraphs with high measured sensitivity can be duplicated/inserted into new graphs as modules
mechanisms.what_can_learn: an observer model learns to predict the sensitivity field from graph structure alone without running propagation
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the mapping from local edge-weight patterns to sensitivity contribution transfers to differently-sized graphs
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: measure whether downstream variance decays with graph distance in a structured (edge-weight-dependent) versus uniform exponential pattern; the mechanism predicts variance concentrated near high-weight paths, a null diffusion model predicts uniform radial decay
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 20-node random DAG with assigned edge weights; intervention perturbs a single source node's value by +/-delta and records propagated node values. The null twin uses the same graph but replaces directed weighted propagation with symmetric random diffusion (same total variance injected, same node count) so aggregate variance statistics match but the causal directionality/attenuation structure is destroyed.

mechanisms.statement: The organism maintains two internal generative models built under different simplifying assumptions (misspecified in complementary ways) and produces its output only from the subspace where both models' predictions agree within tolerance. Disagreement regions are flagged as unreliable and suppressed from action selection.
mechanisms.what_changes: each timestep both models produce predictions; agreement mask updates by thresholding |predA - predB|; only masked-agree outputs are passed to the action module
mechanisms.what_persists: the two models' parameters persist and are independently updated from feedback
mechanisms.what_is_selected: action policies that rely only on agreement-region outputs are favored when a downstream reward signal is compared across organisms with vs without masking
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the dual-model architecture (both parameter sets and masking rule) is copied wholesale to offspring
mechanisms.what_can_learn: each of the two models learns from environment feedback independently, and the disagreement threshold itself is tuned by reward
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the masking policy (which regions to trust) transfers to novel environments sharing structure with training environments
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: under an injected model-misspecification (e.g., changing an unobserved confounder), the dual-model organism's action variance should stay low while a single-model organism's action variance spikes; measure output variance ratio between architectures under the same misspecification shock
mechanisms.minimal_world: A gridworld with a hidden confounding variable affecting reward; model A assumes the confounder is constant, model B assumes it follows a different (wrong) trend. Intervention: abruptly changes the true confounder dynamics. Null twin: a single-model organism using only model A's predictions with no masking, matched in total parameter count by giving it an equivalently sized single network, so only the dual-model comparison and masking mechanism differs.

mechanisms.statement: The learning objective adds a penalty term proportional to the norm of the output's derivative with respect to each input, driving optimization toward parameter regions where outputs are locally flat (robust) rather than merely low-loss. This is distinct from weight-norm regularization because it directly penalizes measured input-sensitivity rather than parameter magnitude.
mechanisms.what_changes: theta updates via gradient of L(theta) + lambda*S(theta), where S is estimated by sampling small random input perturbations each step
mechanisms.what_persists: lambda (the sensitivity-penalty weight) persists across training as a hyperparameter, and the running estimate of S is smoothed
mechanisms.what_is_selected: among many training runs with different lambda, runs whose held-out performance is most stable under test-time input noise are selected
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the penalty schedule (lambda value and estimation procedure) can be copied to new training runs on new tasks
mechanisms.what_can_learn: theta learns to occupy flat regions of the loss landscape; a meta-learner can additionally learn to set lambda from task statistics
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: flat-region parameters transfer better to shifted test distributions than sharp-region parameters trained without the penalty
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: under test-time input corruption of increasing magnitude, measure the slope of output-error vs corruption magnitude; the sensitivity-penalized model should show a shallower slope than a matched-loss model without the penalty, even when both have identical training-set accuracy
mechanisms.minimal_world: A small feedforward regressor trained on noiseless data; intervention adds Gaussian noise to test inputs at increasing variance. Null twin: identical network trained with L2 weight decay tuned to match final training loss exactly, but without the explicit derivative penalty, so the two models are indistinguishable on clean training data but differ under input perturbation.

mechanisms.statement: The system maintains an explicit low-rank matrix representation of its own input-output sensitivity (a running Jacobian estimate), updated online from paired perturbation-response observations, and this matrix is used as a first-class object for downstream control gain-setting rather than being recomputed from scratch each time.

mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a J_hat learned on one system transfers as a good initialization for a related system sharing subspace structure

mechanisms.minimal_world: A linear system y = Ax with A having rank-2 structure embedded in a 20-dimensional input space; intervention presents novel perturbation directions not seen in initial calibration. Null twin: a full-rank unstructured Jacobian estimator (dense finite-difference table) matched in total number of perturbation samples used, which lacks the low-rank inductive bias and thus generalizes worse to novel directions despite equal data.

mechanisms.statement: The organism stores a ledger of past (perturbation, output-delta) pairs indexed by context, and estimates local sensitivity at a new point by weighted nearest-neighbor recall from the ledger instead of recomputing derivatives, trading exact computation for fast approximate robustness checks.

mechanisms.what_changes: on each query, retrieve k nearest stored triples by context similarity, weight-average their delta-output/perturbation ratios to estimate local sensitivity; ledger grows by appending new triples, with oldest/least-used entries evicted when capacity is reached
mechanisms.what_persists: the ledger contents persist across the organism's lifetime subject to eviction policy
mechanisms.what_is_selected: eviction policies (recency vs frequency vs diversity-based) are compared for which yields the most accurate sensitivity recall under a fixed ledger size
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the ledger and retrieval mechanism can be transplanted wholesale to a new organism instance
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the similarity kernel bandwidth and k (number of neighbors) are tuned by feedback on recall accuracy
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: ledger entries from one task context transfer to speed up sensitivity estimation in a related but novel context sharing partial structure
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: measure sensitivity-estimation accuracy versus number of live recomputations required; ledger-based recall should achieve comparable accuracy to direct finite-difference computation while requiring far fewer fresh perturbation trials, especially in contexts resembling previously visited ones
mechanisms.minimal_world: A simulated agent operating in a context space where local sensitivity varies smoothly; intervention introduces a novel context that partially overlaps with previously visited regions. Null twin: an agent that recomputes local sensitivity from scratch via fresh finite-difference sampling every query, matched in total number of environment interactions, but without any persistent ledger, so it cannot benefit from prior overlapping experience.

mechanisms.statement: Mutation rate applied to each genome parameter is scaled inversely to that parameter's measured phenotypic sensitivity (how much small changes to it perturb fitness-relevant output), producing mutational canalization: high-sensitivity parameters are protected from mutation while low-sensitivity ones are freely explored.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: individuals with higher fitness are selected to reproduce; over generations this indirectly selects for genomes whose high-sensitivity parameters have converged to good values
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: genomes reproduce with the sensitivity-scaled mutation operator applied to offspring

mechanisms.what_can_transfer: a canalized genome transplanted into a new but related fitness landscape retains protection on its previously-high-sensitivity parameters, biasing subsequent evolution

mechanisms.minimal_world: A toy genome of 30 parameters mapping through a fixed nonlinear function to a scalar fitness; intervention knocks out (zeroes) one random parameter after 200 generations of evolution and measures fitness drop. mechanisms.statement: Each layer in a hierarchy sends predictions downward and receives residual prediction errors upward; local synaptic weights update only from the locally available error signal, not a global loss. Over time this drives the hierarchy to represent generative causes at increasingly abstract levels, since only structure that reduces layer-local surprise persists.
mechanisms.what_changes: weights update proportional to the product of local error and presynaptic activity (Hebbian-style delta rule); no global backprop signal crosses layer boundaries
mechanisms.what_persists: weight configurations that consistently reduce local prediction error across the training distribution
mechanisms.what_is_selected: connection patterns minimizing residual error variance at each layer
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a layer's predictive template can be copied to initialize a new layer facing structurally similar input statistics
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the mapping from lower-layer activity to predicted lower-layer activity, i.e. a generative model of the layer below
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: higher-layer predictive templates transfer to novel inputs sharing the same generative causes but different surface statistics
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: lesioning only top-down prediction connections (not bottom-up) should collapse high-layer selectivity to noise even though bottom-up pathways are intact, unlike a purely feedforward feature detector which would be unaffected
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 2D grid world generates images from a small set of latent shapes and lighting angles fed through a 3-layer network with top-down/bottom-up connections per the rule above. Intervention: ablate top-down connections after training and measure whether layer-2 units still discriminate shape identity. Null twin: an identical 3-layer feedforward network trained with a single global loss on the same images, matched for parameter count and final reconstruction error, which should show no differential collapse upon top-down ablation since it has no top-down pathway to ablate in the first place — the comparison is between models with vs without a true two-way predictive loop of matched capacity.

mechanisms.statement: A representation layer is forced through a channel of limited capacity (bits or dimensions) positioned between input and a downstream task signal, with an explicit pressure to minimize mutual information with the input while maximizing mutual information with the task label. This produces representations that discard input variance uncorrelated with any future task, i.e. invariances emerge from compression, not from architecture.
what_exists: bottleneck variable Z with a capacity budget
an encoder p(Z|X) and decoder p(Y|Z)
mechanisms.what_changes: encoder/decoder parameters update to trade off I(Z;X) against I(Z;Y) via a Lagrange-weighted objective
mechanisms.what_persists: the minimal sufficient statistic of X for predicting Y, once capacity is low enough to force compression
mechanisms.what_is_selected: encodings that lie on the information-bottleneck frontier for the current task distribution
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: a trained bottleneck encoder can be cloned as an initialization for a new downstream task
mechanisms.what_can_learn: the sufficient-statistic mapping X→Z for whatever Y is currently supervising it
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: Z transfers to novel tasks Y' whenever Y' is predictable from the same sufficient statistic as Y, but not otherwise
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: sweeping the capacity budget downward should produce a measurable, monotonic drop in nuisance-variable decodability from Z while task-relevant decodability stays flat until a sharp threshold — a plain autoencoder (no task term) would show nuisance decodability staying high regardless of capacity
mechanisms.minimal_world: Inputs are images of a shape (task-relevant) rendered with random background color (nuisance). Train an encoder-bottleneck-decoder to predict shape identity under a shrinking bottleneck width. Intervention: vary bottleneck width and measure a linear probe's ability to recover background color from Z. Null twin: an autoencoder with the same bottleneck width trained to reconstruct the full image (no task supervision), matched in width and training data, which should retain background decodability at all widths since it has no pressure to discard task-irrelevant information.

mechanisms.statement: An organism maintains a small set of internal state variables (e.g. energy, damage) that must stay within a bounded viable range; action selection is driven purely by the current deviation of these variables from their setpoints, not by an externally defined reward. Behavior is instrumental to the regulation, so goal-directedness emerges from the geometry of the viability boundary rather than from a hand-coded objective.

mechanisms.what_changes: s decays each timestep by a metabolic cost and jumps upward when a resource is consumed; action policy updates to reduce expected time-to-boundary-violation
mechanisms.what_persists: policies that keep s within bounds indefinitely (viable trajectories)
mechanisms.what_is_selected: action sequences that minimize the frequency or severity of boundary excursions
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: an organism whose s stays viable long enough can spawn an offspring policy with small perturbations
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a value estimate of state-action pairs with respect to distance from the viability boundary, without any externally specified reward scalar
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the boundary-avoidance policy transfers to new resource layouts as long as the viability geometry (bounds, decay rate) is unchanged
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: removing the external reward signal entirely (leaving only s-dynamics) should still produce foraging behavior with statistics matching the reward-trained condition; a reward-driven RL agent with reward set to zero should instead show no directed behavior at all
mechanisms.minimal_world: A grid world with energy that decays 1/step and resource tiles that add energy; agent dies if energy leaves [0,100]. Intervention: strip any external reward signal and let the agent act purely to avoid boundary violation (measured via an internal control loop, not backprop reward). Null twin: an RL agent in the identical grid given reward = +1 for eating, trained to convergence, matched for final survival rate — behavioral divergence under resource scarcity (e.g. risk-taking near the boundary) distinguishes homeostatic control from reward-shaped policy.

This solves temporal credit assignment without backpropagation through time or a value function.

mechanisms.what_is_selected: synapses whose activation reliably precedes reward by less than the trace decay window
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: not applicable at synapse level; at population level, trace-decay time constants can be duplicated across successful agents

mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the learned association transfers to any task sharing the same delay structure between cue and reward
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: varying the cue-to-reward delay should produce a sharp learning-curve degradation once delay exceeds the trace time constant 1/(1-λ), whereas a model using only instantaneous Hebbian updates (no trace) should fail to learn at any nonzero delay, not show a graded threshold
mechanisms.minimal_world: A corridor task: agent presses a lever at position A, reward delivered k steps later at position B, k varied across trials. Intervention: sweep k and measure learning success with the eligibility-trace rule. Null twin: identical network with the trace term removed (Δw = η × r(t) × instantaneous activity only), matched in learning rate and architecture, which should learn only at k=0 and fail catastrophically for any k>0 rather than degrading gradually.

mechanisms.what_persists: the subset of learned dependencies that hold under do(X=x) for all x, i.e. the true causal parents of each variable
mechanisms.what_is_selected: predictive submodels that remain accurate specifically on held-out novel interventions, not just held-out observations
mechanisms.what_can_reproduce: the causal submodel for one variable can be reused unchanged when composing a new graph that shares that variable's parents
mechanisms.what_can_learn: a structural mapping from parent variables to child variable that is invariant to which distribution (observational or interventional) generated the training data
mechanisms.what_can_transfer: the learned causal submodel transfers correctly to entirely new intervention values not seen during training, and to new graphs sharing the same local structure
mechanisms.distinguishing_observable: prediction accuracy under a novel intervention value (not seen in training) should remain high for the flagged causal model, while a purely correlational model trained only on observational data (or trained without the do/observe flag distinguishing the two data sources) should show accuracy collapse specifically on interventional test cases despite matching observational accuracy
mechanisms.minimal_world: A 4-variable synthetic causal graph (e.g. A→B, A→C, B→D, C→D) generates observational data plus data from randomized interventions on single variables. Intervention: train two models — one with the do/observe flag and interventional training data, one purely observational — then test both on prediction under a held-out intervention value on B. Null twin: a model trained on a mixture of observational and interventional data but WITHOUT the do/observe flag (data pooled indistinguishably, matched sample count and variable coverage) — this null twin will fit spurious correlations between B and its non-descendant C that the flagged model correctly avoids, producing systematically worse held-out interventional accuracy despite identical training data content.
